articles.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill several despite truce
articles.summary: Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun has appealed to the international community to "take immediate action to stop these violations" of the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon.

image.caption: One of the buildings that was destroyed was a home in Arab Salim villageImage: Mohammed Zaatari/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: At least four people were killed in Israeli strikes on Lebanon on Sunday, which comes despite a ceasefire between the two countries, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry.
The Lebanese officials also said around 20 other people, including children, were wounded in the strikes.
The office of Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun called the strikes a "dangerous escalation" that targeted "purely civilian administrations and health centers."

"President Aoun held the Israeli side fully responsible for this ongoing escalation, calling on the United States and the international community to take immediate action to stop ​these violations and hold the perpetrators accountable," his aides said in a statement.
In turn, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said the strikes were a response to "a blatant violation" by Hezbollah militants.

"Terrorists from the Hezbollah terrorist organization launched two drones towards IDF soldiers operating in the Security Zone in southern Lebanon," the military said in a statement, adding that there were no reports of Israeli soldiers wounded.
What do we know about the strikes?
Early on Sunday morning, the Israeli military issued an online evacuation alert for Arab Salim, saying it identified a "Hezbollah facility" there.
Lebanon's state-run National News Agency (NNA) said the Israeli military subsequently carried out a strike on the building mentioned in the original evacuation warning.
NNA also reported that "enemy warplanes launched a strike on another house, destroying it." Two women were killed in the strike.

blocks.caption: Two women were reportedly killed by Israeli strikes on Arab Salim villageImage: Mohammed Zaatari/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Another two people were killed in Israeli strikes near the town of Nabatieh al-Fawqa, which lies on the edge of Israel's "security zone" that it occupies in southern Lebanon.
Lebanon's Health Ministry said an Israeli strike "totally destroyed" a disused hospital. The Health Ministry called the incident "another grave violation of international humanitarian law."
The Israeli military said its targets included what it described as a Hezbollah command center inside a building that was previously used as a hospital, as well as a weapons depot.
"The strikes were carried out in response to Hezbollah’s attempted attack yesterday in the Ali Taher Ridge area and to remove threats posed by Hezbollah," it said.

articles.title: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano erupts, cancelling flights at Jakarta airport and others
articles.summary: Anak Krakatau volcano erupted in Indonesia early Sunday, prompting the cancellation of all flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and disrupting other domestic airports as volcanic…

image.caption: Anak Krakatau spews volcanic smoke in Sunda Strait, Indonesia, on Saturday, in this drone photo released by the Geological Agency of Indonesia's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources. (Badan Geologi/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

Anak Krakatau volcano erupted in Indonesia early Sunday, prompting the cancellation of all flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and disrupting other domestic airports as volcanic ash drifted across parts of western Indonesia.
Volcanic ash spread across parts of Jakarta and Lampung province on Sumatra’s southern tip

Anak Krakatau volcano erupted in Indonesia early Sunday, prompting the cancellation of all flights at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and disrupting other domestic airports as volcanic ash drifted across parts of western Indonesia.

The volcanic island located in Indonesia's Sunda Strait between the main Java and Sumatra islands had showed signs of activity since Friday before erupting for 30 seconds at 3:53 a.m. local time Sunday and for 16 seconds about three hours later, Indonesia's Geological Agency said. Closed-circuit camera footage showed lava flares from the volcano.

No casualties were reported, and no evacuation order was issued. The nearest settlement is more than 16 kilometres away, but authorities warned residents and visitors to stay at least three kilometres from the active crater.
Volcanic ash spread across parts of Jakarta and Lampung province on Sumatra's southern tip, Indonesia's Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation said.

AirNav Indonesia closed airspace around Soekarno-Hatta and Halim Perdanakusuma airports in Jakarta, as well as six other airports, including Radin Inten II airport in Lampung, because of volcanic ash.
Thousands of passengers affected
By Sunday evening local time, the closure had affected 467 flights in Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta airport alone that affected about 150,000 passengers. The airport was ordered closed until 11:59 p.m.
"It’s of course an inconvenience," said Diego Urdiales, a Spanish tourist who was supposed to fly home to Madrid. "I was supposed to get input from the airline ... but so far no news."
"It’s a natural disaster, it’s a force majeure, so, what can we do?" said Michele Gouw, an Indonesian passenger. "We just have to accept it and wait for the airline and airport directions."

Indonesia's Directorate General of Civil Aviation said that it was closely monitoring the eruption's impact on air travel and co-ordinating with airlines, airport operators, air navigation services and the meteorology agency.

items: Volcanic eruption in Indonesia forces evacuations, cancelled flights

blocks.text: "Safety remains our top priority in every operational decision," Lukman F. Laisa, director general of civil aviation at the Ministry of Transportation, said in a statement.
He warned flight schedules could face cascading disruptions affecting aircraft rotations, fleet availability and terminal capacity as airlines work to restore operations.
The eruption also disrupted services at Bali’s I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport and at Medan.
Volcano remains active

Indonesia's volcanology agency and the Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre identified two ash clouds using satellite imagery. One plume rose to 6,100 metres and drifted northeast over Jakarta, Banten, West Java and nearby waters. A second cloud reached 15,200 metres and spread over parts of Banten, Lampung and Bengkulu provinces, the southern Sunda Strait and sections of the Indian Ocean west of Sumatra.
Lana Saria, head of Indonesia's Geological Agency, said activity at Anak Krakatau has intensified since July, with Sunday's eruption the strongest during that period.
The repeated eruptions indicate a continued supply of magma and volcanic gases beneath the volcano, she said, though officials can't predict whether a larger eruption will occur.
"We continue to evaluate the volcano's development based on all monitoring data, not solely on the number of eruptions or the height of the ash column," Saria said in a video briefing.
She said the main hazards include volcanic ash, high concentrations of gas and the ejection of hot rocks and other material around the crater area.
Anak Krakatau, which means "child of Krakatau," is the offspring of the famous Krakatau, whose monumental 1883 eruption triggered a period of global cooling.

An eruption of Anak Krakatau in 2018 caused a tsunami that killed at least 430 people in Sumatra and Java. Researchers believe volcanic activity triggered an underwater landslide and caused a large chunk of Anak Krakatau's southwest slope to collapse and displace a large volume of water. Scientists said that Anak Krakatau island was only about a quarter of its original size after that eruption.

articles.title: China prepares £40bn stimulus for financial sector amid fears over sluggish growth
articles.summary:
Beijing wants banks and insurers to bolster investment in stock market as it helps to replenish cash reserves

China will inject $54bn (£40bn) into its financial sector as Beijing attempts to…

blocks.text: China will inject $54bn (£40bn) into its financial sector as Beijing attempts to shore up banks and insurers in the face of faltering economic growth.

A host of financial institutions said they were due to receive billions of yuan in capital from state institutions including the ministry of finance and even the company that runs the country’s tobacco monopoly.

The stimulus is designed to help China bolster the ability of its financial sector to invest in the stock market and lend to businesses, amid signs that the world’s second largest economy is struggling to escape weak growth.
The country’s largest life insurer, China Life Insurance, will get 35bn yuan, while the China Taiping Insurance Group said it would receive 7bn.

The People’s Insurance ⁠Company of China said it planned to raise up to 15bn yuan through a private placement of A-shares – stock that specifically allows investors to trade in China-based companies – to the ministry ​of finance, with the proceeds used to replenish ‌its capital.

The initiative could help bolster ‌state insurers that have been directed by Beijing to support the stock market with medium- and long-term funds, while positioning them to help regulators ‌manage smaller, higher-risk insurance companies.

The insurance sector has been struggling with eroding profitability owing to persistently low interest rates, with numerous small and mid-sized insurers reporting deteriorating solvency ratios, a measure of financial health.

“The injection is an important step by the country to enhance the financial sector’s ability to serve the real economy and promote the high-quality ‌development of the financial and insurance industries,” China Life said, adding that it would strengthen the group’s ability to withstand risk.
Separately, three state lenders on Sunday also announced they will receive a combined 290bn yuan in capital injections.
after newsletter promotion
The plan was first announced at an annual parliamentary meeting in March this year, extending a financing tool that had helped bolster some other big state banks last year.

The Agricultural Bank of China and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, two of the country’s largest state banks, said ⁠they planned to raise up to 160bn yuan and 100bn yuan respectively through private A-share ​placements to the finance ministry, China National Tobacco ​Corp and its subsidiaries.

The two lenders said the ​proceeds would be used entirely to replenish cash reserves, helping them ​sustain credit expansion, as Beijing leans ‌on state banks ​to support growth despite weak demand for loans.

articles.title: Shoebridge criticises Labor response after IDF officer’s ‘reprehensible’ comments on deadly Zomi Frankcom strike
articles.summary: Greens defence spokesman says ‘words are just distractions’ until government takes action

blocks.text: The Greens have criticised inflammatory statements from the former Israel Defense Forces officer who ordered the attack which killed Zomi Frankcom, accusing the Albanese government of weakness over its failure to halt military exports and impose new sanctions.

Australian aid worker Frankcom and six of her colleagues were killed in 2024 while bringing food to the people of Gaza. Former IDF reserve colonel Nochi Mendel has said he would do “exactly the same thing” again and that those killed in the World Central Kitchen (WCK) humanitarian convoy in Gaza were “not innocent”.
The statements have been condemned as “utterly disgraceful” by Australia’s foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, and as an “outrageous smear” by WCK’s humanitarian chief.

But the Greens’ defence spokesperson, David Shoebridge, said the government’s response was insufficient in the face of Mendel’s “reprehensible” statements. He said the comments “reflect the rhetoric and policy of the Israeli government, where collective punishment of aid workers, doctors and innocent civilians is occurring daily”.
“I do not care what minister Wong’s personal feelings are, I don’t care about her outrage, I care about the actions taken as foreign minister,” Shoebridge told Guardian Australia.
“Anyone can condemn the actions of the Israeli military, but only the government can impose the sanctions and material responses needed. Until they do their words are distractions.”
He called for material reprimand for members of Benjamin Netanyahu’s government and for the sale of parts for the F-35 fighter jet to be immediately halted.

blocks.caption: The Greens’ defence spokesperson, David Shoebridge, said on Sunday he could not fathom the pain and distress facing Zomi Frankcom’s family. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP

blocks.text: José Andrés, the WCK founder, said Mendel had smeared Frankcom and her colleagues.
“Now, one of the officers involved says he isn’t sorry for what happened. He said we are not a neutral organisation,” he said in a statement published online this week.
“Really? Let me be very clear, to him and to the whole world. We are humanitarians. We are friends of humanity. We believe that food is a universal human right.”
Mendel, then the chief of staff of the Nahal brigade, said he gave the order to attack a humanitarian convoy delivering hundreds of tonnes of food to Gaza on the night of 1 April 2024.
Three vehicles in the convoy were attacked along Gaza’s coast road, in successive drone strikes, each about two minutes apart.
One after another, the three vehicles were bombed, as survivors from the initial strikes ran to the untouched cars, seeking sanctuary.

An IDF investigation found the attack was a grave mistake, identifying specific errors made by a handful of officers, in particular Mendel, who was removed from his position. The victims of the strike were also blamed for hiring armed guards to protect the food aid convoy and for allegedly “deviating” from their agreed route.
Last month, Israel’s advocate general declined to press charges against anyone for the deaths, saying there was “no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct”.

Mendel has given interviews to the ABC and the Guardian saying he did not regret the attacks. He told the Guardian he was following IDF protocol, and the humanitarians were marked as targets under an Israeli military practice of establishing guilt by association.

Mendel was referring to a general policy of haflala, “incrimination”, which gives commanders in the field wide discretion in designating a person a “terrorist”, including those “incriminated” by association.
Mendel told the Guardian while he didn’t plan to kill aid workers, those killed “were not innocent because they were connected to Hamas”.

He did not support this assertion with any evidence. Investigations by the IDF itself and the former head of the Australian military have found no suggestion of any connection between Hamas and World Central Kitchen.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: A destroyed car from the World Central Kitchen convoy in the southern Gaza Strip. Photograph: Mohammed Saber/EPA

blocks.text: Mendel said he fought in the war in Gaza “to defeat Hamas”, and dismissed the seriousness of the killing of seven humanitarians.
“If such an event came before me again, I would do exactly the same thing,” he told the Guardian.
“I think it’s an idiotic side event. It really isn’t a serious event.”
Wong, asked about earlier comments from Mendel that he was unapologetic over the strikes, said his statements were extremely distressing for Frankcom’s family.
“I thought those comments were disgraceful, utterly disgraceful,” she told the ABC. “I don’t even want to go into some of the detail of them because I don’t want to give them any credence.”
Wong said the Australian government was dissatisfied with Israel’s decision not to lay criminal charges against those responsible, and would continue to “press for justice”.
“We do want to see full accountability for the deaths of Zomi Frankcom and her colleagues. They were humanitarian workers working to deliver aid and they are protected under the Geneva conventions.”

blocks.caption: Wong 'outraged' at Israeli decision to not criminally investigate Zomi Frankcom killing – video

blocks.text: Restaurateur Andrés, whose charity has provided more than 600m meals to people affected by natural disasters, climate emergencies and conflict around the world, said the deaths of humanitarian workers who were just trying to feed hungry people was inexcusable.
“Enough with the outrageous smears. Enough with excuses. Enough with the shifting of blame.

“From the start, we have demanded truth, truth and justice for our friends and their families. We want an independent investigation with all the video and audio released in public so the world can know the truth, because we continue to grieve for our friends. We will never forget them or stop fighting for them.”
Frankcom’s family issued a statement following Israel’s decision not to lay criminal charges, saying they were “deeply disappointed” by the decision.

“The families of the victims deserve transparency and an independent judicial assessment of the criminal responsibility for the international humanitarian law violations that took place on that day,” the said.
Shoebridge said on Sunday he could not fathom the pain and distress facing the Frankcom family.

“I think most people are in shock at the inaction of the Labor government when an Australian has been murdered and the killers walk free. At some point the Albanese government is going to have to get their head out of sand and start taking action.”

articles.title: Volcanic eruption halts flights at Jakarta and seven other Indonesian airports
articles.summary:
Ash cloud from Anak Krakatau affects hundreds of flights and some school and fishing activities

Indonesia halted operations at eight airports on Sunday, including from its main international…

blocks.text: Indonesia halted operations at eight airports on Sunday, including from its main international hub, affecting hundreds of flights as a result of an ash cloud from the Anak Krakatau volcano.
Saturday’s eruption, which produced lava and booming sounds that were heard up to 435 miles (700km) away, according to Indonesia’s geology agency, also interrupted some school activities and fishing.
Two more eruptions were recorded on Sunday.

Ash was detected in the airspace around Soekarno-Hatta international airport near Jakarta, prompting authorities to suspend operations. They announced several extensions of the shutdown, keeping the airport closed to flights until 9.30pm local time on Sunday.

The suspension affected hundreds of flights, including international ones, the airport operator, Angkasa Pura, announced. Singapore Airlines said it had cancelled flights to and from Jakarta for the rest of Sunday.
The Australian flag carrier said there were “disruptions to a number of Qantas services, including cancellations to and from Jakarta today”.
“Our meteorologists and operations teams are closely monitoring conditions in and around Jakarta and any impact on our operations,” it said in a statement.
“Safety remains our highest priority. We have contacted affected customers and are providing assistance. Services will resume when conditions allow.”
Volcanic ash can damage jet engines – baking on to hot internal parts and quickly wearing out turbine blades, as well as clogging fuel and air systems. It can also damage pilots’ windscreens.

blocks.caption: Passengers wait in the check-in lounge at Soekarno-Hatta international airport.  Photograph: Faisal Ramadhan/EPA

blocks.text: Ash ‌reached as high as 6,000 metres (20,000 feet) ‌on the Java side of the volcano and 15,000 metres on the Sumatra side and some parts of Banten province in Java, the meteorological agency BMKG said.
Several ​schools cancelled activities on Saturday after students and residents ​suffered eye irritationand fishers cancelled fishing trips, the local media outlet Kompas reported.
The disaster mitigation agency BNPB said it would conduct a weather modification operation, which could ​include cloud-seeding to promote rain.

“If it rains heavily enough, the volcanic ash that has been disrupting our daily lives since yesterday and continuing today will be washed away quickly,” the BNPB chief, Lt Gen Suharyanto, told a press conference.
More than 22,000 passengers and 209 flights were affected, the transport ministry said, particularly those bound to and from Singapore.
Other affected international routes included Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur.
At least 16 domestic flights to Bali were cancelled, local airport authorities said.

Anak Krakatau, which means “child of Krakatau”, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra. The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea in the caldera formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau. That was one of the deadliest and most destructive volcanic eruptions in human history. About 35,000 people were killed.
Port authorities said ships passing through the strait were prohibited to go within a two-mile radius of the volcano and should be vigilant.
With Agence France-Presse

articles.title: Dozens feared trapped in collapsed building in Delhi
articles.summary: As many as 50 people are thought to have been inside the five-storey hostel when it came down.

blocks.text: Many of the students staying there were thought to be in their rooms at the time of the collapse as there were no lessons on Sunday.
A legislative assembly member said at the scene that some of the trapped students had been making calls from under the rubble.
Eyewitnesses told local media that another building beside the hostel had also collapsed.
Chief Minister of Delhi Rekha Gupta said an adjacent building had been evacuated "as a precautionary measure".
"Every possible effort is being made to safely rescue those trapped," she added.
Delhi Police said the building had only been 40 or 50 years old.
The owner of a nearby shop told news agency ANI that it was under a 100-year lease and that the leaseholder had undertaken excavation work in the basement to increase their income.
"They strengthened the upper building, but the pillars below were weak," he said, noting that the construction workers had also been buried.
The National Students' Union of India called on the government to investigate the cause of the collapse and hold anyone found responsible to account.
"Negligence with the safety of students and common people will not be tolerated at any cost," it said.
Police are searching for the owner of the building, Times of India reports.

articles.title: Nepalese woman found alive days after family began mourning rites following deadly flood
articles.summary: Believing she had perished in Nepal's deadly floods, the family of Chandika Kumari Shrestha started the ritual of mourning the elderly woman's death.

image.caption: Nepal Police officers assist Chandika Kumari Shrestha after she was rescued alive from a damaged house following deadly flash floods and mudslides, in Betrawati, in Nuwakot district, Nepal, on Saturday. (Nepal Police/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
Believing she had perished in Nepal's deadly floods, the family of Chandika Kumari Shrestha started the ritual of mourning the elderly woman's death.
Rescuers found woman alive inside her collapsed home in the devastated Betrawati village
Ten days later, rescuers found her alive inside her collapsed home in the devastated Betrawati village, where she had survived in a narrow pocket of air amid water and mud.

"The four-storey house was swept [away] by the floods and the house was left in the middle of a quicksand. While walking around it, we heard a voice [say] 'save me,'" police officer Mahendra Darnal said.
In a rescue operation on Saturday lasting 45 minutes, Darnal and his team found Shrestha in a confined space and sent her to an army hospital.
"I was in touch with the family, and they had started the 11-day mourning period," Darnal said.

Shrestha was among the hundreds missing in Betrawati, an area among the hardest hit by the floods in Nepal and engulfed with white deposits compacted almost like concrete. Crews continue to recover scores of dead bodies.

The town's market and most residential buildings, some as tall as four storeys, were almost completely buried under debris left by a torrent that swept through the valley, part of a disaster that killed more than 1,300 people across Nepal. Thousands remain unaccounted for.

items: Rescuers in Nepal pull 2 people alive from the debris 10 days after devastating floods

blocks.text: Rescue workers wearing hard hats were seen digging with shovels, while some were crawling through the gaps of collapsed buildings periodically blowing whistles to get the attention of anyone trapped and alive.
Five days earlier, 24 bodies were found in a decomposed state in Betrawati's market area in a building that had contained a small shop, Darnal said.
Looking for signs of life
Eleven days since a glacial collapse triggered the devastating floods, close to 5,000 are still missing.

Hundreds of bodies have been swept onto the banks of rivers far from the ravaged Rasuwa district. In Chitwan, hundreds of kilometres away, several rounds of mass burials have taken place for unidentified and badly decomposed bodies.

items: More than 1,000 dead from catastrophic Nepal-China floods as rescuers search for survivors
Hopes of finding survivors dim a week after catastrophic Nepal flood

blocks.text: Even as hope is beginning to fade, Nepal authorities continue their effort to look for people stuck in tunnels and under the thick deposits of mud that have hardened over buildings.
Since Friday, they have pulled out three people from the tunnels, including a Chinese citizen by the Trishuli river, where more than 900 are believed to be trapped.
Others like Shrestha have survived in extraordinary conditions, including an eight-year-old boy who was also reunited with his mother.

articles.title: Iran threatens greater force if US launches more attacks
articles.summary: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran’s top negotiator on Sunday threatened a more forceful response to any further US attacks after Tehran targeted American warships in their latest round of clashes. The…

blocks.text: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran’s top negotiator on Sunday threatened a more forceful response to any further US attacks after Tehran targeted American warships in their latest round of clashes.
The exchanges of fire, which began with US raids last week, come amid a deadlock in the six-month war between the two sides.
Iran has maintained its stranglehold on the strategic Strait of Hormuz while Washington continues a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
Washington is also seeking to choke Iran’s economy, rolling out sanctions on entities with financial links to the Islamic Republic in a bid to force it into submission.

“The Americans must have understood that the era of proportionate responses has come to an end,” said Iran’s parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has acted as chief negotiator in talks to end the war.
“Any aggression against Iran’s interests and security will receive a faster, more intense and more painful response,” he added, in a speech carried by state media.

On Saturday, US Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees American military operations in the region, said Iran had unsuccessfully fired at two American warships — an aircraft carrier and a destroyer.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said the warships had been “forced to retreat” after “suffering damage”, but CENTCOM said they successfully evaded the attacks.
In response, the US military said it struck three oil tankers linked to the Iranian Guards.
“Following Iran’s failed attacks, CENTCOM permanently disabled the IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask,” CENTCOM said.

“American forces also completely destroyed the unladen crude oil carrier M/T Kylo… in the Gulf of Oman, striking the vessel in multiple critical locations to render it inoperable after the crew was directed to abandon ship.”
Video posted by CENTCOM showed large fireballs and billowing flames after projectiles slammed into the ships.
The three vessels were “part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies,” CENTCOM said.

Iran quickly retaliated, with the Guards saying their naval forces “targeted three oil tankers on the unauthorized route of the Strait of Hormuz and three vessels affiliated with the child-killing America in other areas.”
It warned ships not to attempt to transit the key trade waterway via routes unapproved by Tehran.
Early on Sunday, Iran’s Guards also said they attacked a US naval drone trying to enter the strait, according to a statement carried by state television.
‘Higher economic cost’
CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said after the exchange of strikes: “If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours.”
The Iranian Foreign Ministry hit out at Washington over the attacks on its oil tankers, calling them “illegal and aggressive actions.”

A correspondent for Iranian state TV in Jask in the southern province of Hormozgan said one of the tankers was empty and the second was carrying oil. The crews were transported to shore on lifeboats, they said.
Another state TV correspondent on Kharg Island said the attack there caused no casualties.
The administration of US President Donald Trump has tried to downplay the significance of the six-month conflict, which has proven increasingly unpopular at home as midterm elections near.
US Vice President JD Vance has gone so far as to say that he “wouldn’t call it a war.”
Trump reiterated that view on Friday, calling the war “small potatoes” for Washington.
Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned this week that the Islamic Republic had adopted a “new strategy” against Washington that “will shatter your foundations.”
The US has been trying to step up pressure on Tehran in a bid to wrestle control of the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies previously flowed.
A fragile ceasefire between the two sides collapsed in July after attacks on commercial ships in the waterway.
Trump has in recent weeks repeatedly threatened to claim sovereignty over the strait, even posting a map showing it as “new US territory.”
Vance has insisted the US will not reopen talks with Iran until it ends attacks on commercial shipping in the strait.

articles.title: PCSO GM Robles elected APLA vice chair, another 1st for PH
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Melquiades A. Robles, general manager of the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO), has been elected vice chairman of the Asia Pacific Lottery Association (APLA),…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Melquiades A. Robles, general manager of the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO), has been elected vice chairman of the Asia Pacific Lottery Association (APLA), becoming the first Filipino to hold the prestigious leadership position in the regional lottery organization.
Robles was elected during the 2026 APLA General Assembly held from Sept. 1 to 4 in Seoul, South Korea.
The 2026 APLA General Assembly gathered lottery leaders and industry experts from across the region under the theme “Sustainable Gaming and Innovation, New Trends.”
Discussions covered responsible gaming policies, emerging technologies, sustainable lottery operations, and evolving global industry trends.
“This is not only a personal honor but, more importantly, a recognition of the Philippines and the meaningful work being undertaken by PCSO,” Robles said.
“Through this position, we hope to contribute more actively to regional cooperation, responsible gaming, innovation, and the use of lottery revenues to uplift communities.”
His election marks another historic milestone for the Philippines in the international lottery sector, according to a PCSO statement issued on Sunday.
In September 2024, Robles became the first Filipino elected to the APLA Executive Committee during the association’s Regional Conference in Hanoi, Vietnam.
Responsible lottery operations

His election as vice chairman, for which he will serve a two-year term until 2028, reflected the growing recognition of the transparency and integrity of the Philippines and the PCSO among lottery organizations in the Asia-Pacific region, as well as the country’s commitment to transparent, ethical, and responsible lottery operations.
Under Robles’ leadership, PCSO advanced from Level 1 to Level 3 accreditation under the World Lottery Association’s Responsible Gaming Framework in a record three years.

This feat demonstrates how PCSO translated its commitment to responsible gaming into structured programs, dedicated resources, player-protection measures, and internationally aligned practices focused on integrity and ethical operations.

Founded in 2000, APLA is one of the five regional associations of the World Lottery Association. It represents lottery operators and industry partners from the Asia-Pacific region and provides a platform through which members exchange knowledge, share international best practices, and work together on issues affecting the global lottery industry.
The association has 21 full members from 12 countries and 26 associate members from 13 countries across Asia, Europe, and North America.
Stronger voice

Robles’ election gives PCSO and the Philippines a stronger voice in discussions on responsible gaming, technological innovation, lottery security, industry integrity, and the use of lottery-generated funds for public benefit.
It also creates further opportunities for PCSO to learn from international best practices and share its experience as a government lottery institution with a distinct charitable and social mandate.

The APLA and the World Lottery Association promote responsible gaming, which seeks to ensure that lottery games are conducted fairly, safely, and transparently while protecting players, particularly minors and vulnerable individuals, from the potential risks associated with excessive gambling.
Responsible gaming measures include the following:

items: age restrictions,
clear information for players
spending and play controls
self-exclusion mechanisms
access to appropriate support services=

blocks.text: “Lotteries must always be operated with responsibility and a clear public purpose. Our role is not simply to generate revenues but to ensure that these resources are translated into healthcare assistance, social services, and other programs that improve people’s lives,” Robles said.

APLA also recognizes the important contribution of lotteries to society and good causes. Across the region, member organizations use lottery proceeds to support healthcare, education, community development, sports, culture, disaster response, charitable initiatives, and other social programs.

This closely aligns with PCSO’s mandate as the Philippine government’s principal charity arm. Revenues generated from its lottery and sweepstakes operations help finance medical assistance, health-related programs, mandatory contributions to national government initiatives, support for local government units, and assistance to communities affected by calamities and other emergencies.

“PCSO’s participation in APLA allows us to bring home valuable lessons from other jurisdictions while also showing the international community how lottery revenues can become a meaningful instrument for charity and nation-building,” Robles added.

articles.title: 5 witnesses left in VP secret funds scrutiny – prosec
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution hopes to wrap up its presentation on the alleged misuse of confidential funds of Vice President Sara Duterte by Wednesday, as it has only five remaining…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution hopes to wrap up its presentation on the alleged misuse of confidential funds of Vice President Sara Duterte by Wednesday, as it has only five remaining witnesses who have been subpoenaed, according to lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro.
In a statement on Sunday, Luistro listed the five remaining witnesses:

items: former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer (SDO) Edward Fajarda
his wife, DepEd Assistant Secretary Sunshine Charry Fajarda
Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande
Police Maj. Jovelyn Magay
Commission on Audit (COA) employee Bresilio Sabaldan among the remaining witnesses

blocks.text: The first impeachment article accuses the vice president of misuse, misappropriation,n and irregular liquidation of P612.5 million in confidential funds — P500 million under the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and P112.5 million under DepEd during her tenure as education secretary until 2024.
The prosecution expects to focus this partly on the DepEd funds, which were released in three P37.5-million tranches in 2023.

But the appearance of Edward Fajarda, who served as DepEd’s SDO for the funds, remained uncertain after he suffered a stroke, which was independently confirmed by the Senate Medical and Dental Bureau.
According to Luistro, the prosecution is exploring stipulations with Duterte’s defense that could allow it to dispense with Fajarda’s testimony.
“It is our intention not to aggravate his condition. As a matter of fact, it is likewise our intention to excuse him, if possible, from the rigors of being presented in the witness stand,” she said.

Last Wednesday, defense lawyer Michael Wesley Poa, former DepEd undersecretary, chief of staff, and spokesperson, testified that he learned during a 2024 House inquiry that Fajarda had turned over all three P37.5-million confidential fund releases to then-DepEd security officer Col. Dennis Nolasco.
Grande is expected to testify on PSA records as the prosecution scrutinizes identities appearing in acknowledgment receipts submitted to support confidential fund liquidations.
The prosecution has already presented Commission on Audit auditors, OVP, and DepEd officials, and military officers to the court to trace how the funds were handled and liquidated.

Among these witnesses, former OVP SDO Gina Acosta testified that she turned over four P125-million confidential fund tranches to then-security chief Col. Raymund Dante Lachica upon Duterte’s instruction.

Army officers also testified that their units received no DepEd confidential funds for Youth Leadership Summits and information campaigns cited in military certifications later used by DepEd in responding to COA findings.

The prosecution has since dropped Lachica, Nolasco, and Ramil Madriaga — Duterte’s alleged bagman — as witnesses after concluding that evidence already presented was sufficient for the points it sought to establish.

As part of their effort to speed up the trial, prosecutors are also considering whether to proceed with the third impeachment article, which accuses Duterte of bribery, but they have not made a final decision. /atm

articles.title: Dropping bribery rap in VP trial no issue; 1 article enough to convict – Tolosa
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte may still be convicted in her impeachment case even if the bribery charge against her were to be dropped, as one article would be enough for that…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte may still be convicted in her impeachment case even if the bribery charge against her were to be dropped, as one article would be enough for that decision, according to prosecution counsel Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr.

Tolosa made that statement during the Saturday News Forum at Dapo Restaurant in Quezon City, stressing that each of the four articles of impeachment stands on its own — and only one article needs to be proven for the vice president to be convicted and penalized with removal from her post and perpetual disqualification from public office.
She need not be found guilty in all of the impeachment articles, Tolosa added.

As part of efforts to shorten the trial, the prosecution has been considering whether to drop the third impeachment article, which accuses Duterte of bribery involving alleged monetary gifts or payments to Department of Education officials during her tenure as education secretary until 2024.
The prosecution has not made a final decision, as it was still studying the possibility, along with the feasibility of reducing the number of witnesses.
Article I accuses Duterte of the alleged misuse, misappropriation, and irregular liquidation of P612.5 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President and Department of Education.
Article II involves allegations of unexplained wealth, incomplete disclosure of assets, and continued business interests.
Article IV concerns Duterte’s alleged grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former Speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez.

The prosecution has already rested its presentation on the fourth article and is currently completing its evidence on the first article, with prosecutors earlier aiming to wrap up their presentation on Sept. 9.

According to a prosecution statement, the withdrawal of an impeachment article, if it should be decided, would not be unprecedented. In the 2012 impeachment trial of the late Chief Justice Renato Corona, five of the eight articles originally transmitted to the Senate were withdrawn.

The Senate convicted Corona on one article involving his statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth, demonstrating that an impeachment judgment does not require conviction on every charge brought before the tribunal. /atm

articles.title: No bailouts for Jaguar Land Rover amid reports of thousands of job cuts, says minister
articles.summary:
Carmaker, which is battling Trump tariffs and Chinese competitors, faces talks with union leaders and government

The government has signalled that it will not invest taxpayers’ money to…

blocks.text: The government has signalled that it will not invest taxpayers’ money to limit job losses at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), after it emerged that the UK’s biggest carmaker is planning up to 4,000 redundancies.
Before crunch talks on Tuesday between JLR, union leaders and government officials, the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said it was not his job to “intervene and run businesses”.

JLR, owned by the Indian conglomerate Tata Motors, told staff on Friday to expect a voluntary redundancy programme, as it tries to shore itself up against tough conditions with £1.7bn in cuts over two years.
The Coventry-based company is expected to provide further details on job cuts as soon as Monday, which could include an admission that compulsory job losses are possible.
The expected cuts, which represent almost 12% of JLR’s 34,000-strong UK workforce, threaten to provide an early reality check on Andy Burnham’s pledge to “reindustrialise” Britain.

blocks.caption: Jaguar Land Rover staff check Range Rover bodies at the carmaker’s factory in Solihull. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

blocks.text: Sources said they expect the redundancies, first reported in the Sunday Times, to be weighted towards more senior roles in management and research and development rather than shop floor production workers.
JLR is understood to be responding to pressure from Tata to offset a slump in sales, exacerbated by the fallout from last year’s cyber-attack and the impact of Donald Trump’s tariff wars.
Speaking on the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg show on Sunday, Reynolds signalled that the government was unwilling to put money into the business to limit job losses.
Asked if there could be financial support to protect the jobs, he said: “Not if it’s to bail people out.

“If this is about making sure over time that workforce is right to make the business as ⁠competitive as possible, that’s the conversation we need to have,” Reynolds said, referring to the wider “challenging” environment for the auto sector.
“We need to adapt to evolving global market conditions,” a spokesperson for JLR, which has its largest plant in Solihull in the West Midlands, said.

Reynolds is expected to come under pressure to help staunch the number of job cuts from the Unite general secretary, Sharon Graham, during crunch talks with the JLR chief executive, PB Balaji, scheduled for Tuesday. Union officials will push for JLR to swerve compulsory job losses in favour of retraining or voluntary redundancy where possible.
While Reynolds indicated that no bailout would be available, he hinted at other options to support carmakers.

He refused to rule out watering down government targets for UK automakers to reach 80% zero-emission car sales by 2030, which would lead to a ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel cars by 2035, pointing to an open consultation on the issue.
Carmakers and unions have lobbied hard for a slower transition, saying the targets outpace actual customer demand.
Reynolds also said that the government was sometimes prepared to invest “alongside” industry.

In 2024, the new Labour government under Keir Starmer agreed to invest £500m in another Tata business, the Port Talbot steelworks, to build greener electric arc furnaces. However, the investment did not prevent 2,500 job losses at the south Wales site.

blocks.caption: Stephen Kinnock, the secretary of state for Wales, and Andy Burnham at Tata Steel in Port Talbot – Keir Starmer’s investment in 2024 did not prevent job losses there. Photograph: Simon Dawson/No 10 Downing Street

blocks.text: The prospect of a jobs purge at JLR poses a challenge for Burnham, who has placed plans to “reindustrialise” Britain at the heart of his offer to voters since taking office less than two months ago.

Last year, after JLR suffered the crippling cyber-attack, the government agreed to provide the company with a guaranteed loan facility of £1.5bn to help battle the impact on its supply chains and production. None of the loan has been drawn down.

As well as the cyber-attack, which halted production for several weeks and dented the UK economy, JLR has suffered the fallout from tariffs imposed by Trump, affecting the key American market for models such as the Range Rover and Defender.

Trump initially slapped tariffs of 27.5% on British cars before reducing the figure to 10% as part of a US-UK trade deal unveiled by Starmer to great fanfare at a press conference held at JLR’s Solihull plant in May last year.
Competition from Chinese models such as ​the Jaecoo 7 – ​ranked third among Britain’s top-selling cars – ​has also eaten into sales at JLR, which makes more than 400,000 vehicles a year.

JLR is not alone in being affected by these external factors. The German carmaker Volkswagen said last week it plans to cut a further 50,000 jobs as part of its turnaround plan as it faces US tariffs and Chinese competition.
The Guardian has approached the department for business and trade for comment.

articles.title: German startup sends first commercial rocket into space from Europe
articles.summary:
Isar Aerospace plans rapid expansion amid race to capitalise on expanding satellite-launch market

A German startup has launched the first commercial rocket to reach orbit from continental…

blocks.text: A German startup has launched the first commercial rocket to reach orbit from continental Europe, a milestone for Europe’s efforts to secure independent access to space.

Isar Aerospace said on Sunday that it would rapidly ⁠expand satellite deployments after the ⁠first orbital launch of ​its uncrewed Spectrum rocket from Arctic Norway, marking a ⁠breakthrough for a region where several countries are seeking a foothold in the fast-growing market for satellite launches.
“Launch capability is right now the biggest bottleneck in the entire industry,” Isar co-founder and CEO Daniel Metzler told reporters.
Friedrich Merz, the German chancellor, hailed Saturday’s launch in a ​statement, calling it “the beginning of a new era”.

Merz visited Isar’s ‌launch site in March, underscoring Europe’s ‌efforts to establish greater autonomy as the global order once championed by the US is shifting under the administration of country’s president, Donald Trump.
The EU defence and space commissioner, Andrius Kubilius, wrote on the social media platform X: “Europe’s independent access to space just got a major boost.”
Blasting off from Andøya Spaceport, Spectrum carried five small satellites along with an in-flight technology experiment.
It was Isar’s second launch, coming 18 months after the company’s first rocket plunged into the sea and exploded in a fiery spectacle shortly after takeoff from the same site.
Isar has said it already has five more rockets in production and is now focused on scaling up operations to meet rising demand, with a long-term goal of conducting about 40 launches a year.
The German company ​is developing a second launch site in Nova Scotia in eastern Canada.

Global players ⁠in the satellite launch market include Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which launches from the US, and the French firm ArianeGroup, ​a joint venture between Airbus and Safran ​that uses a spaceport in French Guiana, South America.

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill 4 in southern Lebanon
articles.summary: Israeli strikes killed four people, including two women, in southern Lebanon on Sunday, the Lebanese Health Ministry said, as Israel retaliated for what it said were Hezbollah drone attacks within…

image.caption: Smoke rises in southern Lebanon following Israeli strike in Arab Salim, Lebanon, Sept. 6 , 2026. (Ali Hankir/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Israeli strikes killed four people, including two women, in southern Lebanon on Sunday, the Lebanese Health Ministry said, as Israel retaliated for what it said were Hezbollah drone attacks within areas occupied by its troops.
Lebanon President Joseph Aoun calls attacks 'a dangerous escalation' that destroyed hospital
Despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire with Hezbollah agreed in June, the Israeli military is operating in what it has declared as a security zone in southern Lebanon.

Lebanon's Health Ministry said that two men were killed in a town on the edge of the zone occupied by Israeli troops, while the two women were killed in Arab Salim, which sits well north of the occupied area.

The Israeli military had issued an online evacuation warning at 6 a.m. local time for areas near a building in Arab Salim that it said it would strike because it was being used by Hezbollah. Two girls were among six others injured in that strike.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun's office called Sunday's strikes, which it said destroyed a hospital and damaged a Finance Ministry building, "a dangerous escalation" that targeted "purely civilian administrations and health centres."

"President Aoun held the Israeli side fully responsible for this ongoing escalation, calling on the United States and the international community to take immediate action to stop these violations and hold the perpetrators accountable," Aoun's office said.

The Israeli military said its targets included what it described as Hezbollah weapons storage facilities and a command centre inside a building previously used as a hospital. It also said it used precision munitions and aerial surveillance to mitigate civilian harm.
Sunday's evacuation warning was only the second issued since the June ceasefire announcement.

items: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11, Health Ministry says

blocks.text: The first online evacuation order came on Aug. 5 for residents of Mansouri, near Tyre, though Israel had already dropped leaflets on the village just a week into the ceasefire, telling residents to leave ahead of strikes.

Four people were killed and 23 injured across southern Lebanon on Friday, the Health Ministry said on Saturday, in Israeli strikes launched without evacuation warnings. The Israeli military said those strikes hit Hezbollah weapons storage facilities.

Hezbollah said on Saturday that Israel's continued escalation aimed to pressure the Lebanese government, which has been engaged in direct talks with Israel under U.S. auspices — negotiations that the Iran-backed group has rejected.
More than 4,300 people have been killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon since March 2, when Hezbollah fired at Israel in support of Iran.

articles.title: US envoys Witkoff, Kushner arrive in Kiyv after Putin talks
articles.summary: The two US offcials are meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, with national security advisors the UK, France, and Germany reportedly also in Ukraine for talks.

image.caption: The US envoys met Zelenskyy after talking to Putin in MoscowImage: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS

blocks.text: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner made their first official visit to Ukraine on Sunday as part of fresh efforts toward peace with Russia.

As Ukraine's airspace remains closed due to the conflict, the pair arrived in Kyiv by train from Poland, having spent more than three hours in talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow a day earlier.
Putin had declared a three-day ceasefire to ensure the envoys' safety.
Ukraine peace push? Trump envoys hold talks with Kremlin
Zelenskyy: Ukraine's peace proposals are ready
Ahead of the visit, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote on social media that Kyiv is ready for a “constructive” discussion with its US counterparts.
“We are interested in bringing the end of the war closer," he wrote. "Peace is needed. Security guarantees are needed. A just and sustainable postwar peace is needed. Our proposals are prepared.”
Reuters news agency reported that national security advisors from the United Kingdom, France and Germany were also in Kyiv for talks with the US envoys, citing a source familiar with the matter.
Momentum by US President Donald Trump to end the four-and-a-half-year-old conflict has stalled in recent months after talks with Putin at the Kremlin in January failed to produce a result.
Ukraine's Budanov expects war to continue for many months
Despite hopes of a breakthrough with the Russian leader on Saturday, there were no announcements after the meeting.
Putin’s foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov described the Moscow talks as constructive, frank, and useful but didn’t discuss specific outcomes.
Ushakov said the talks also focused on economic issues and potentially large Russia-US projects.
During previous talks, negotiators have struggled to bring both sides together on a range of key issues, including the future of the industrial Donbas region of eastern Ukraine.

blocks.caption: The US and Russia have been discussing tie-ins for months to try and end the warImage: Sputnik/Kremlin Pool/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: For Ukraine, hard security guarantees from its European allies and Washington are crucial to deterring Russia ​from further aggression.
Kyrylo Budanov, Zelenskyy's chief of staff, told the New York Times last weekend that he did not expect the fighting to end before spring 2027.
He also predicted further Russian strategic air strikes on Ukraine this winter.
The war has escalated in recent months, with Putin seeking the complete conquest of Dombas and Russian drones targeting the Ukrainian capital.
Meanwhile, Ukraine has focused its drone attacks on Russia's energy sector. It has also targeted online retailers deep inside Russia to try and bring the war home to the public.

articles.title: PNP reshuffles 7 officials, names new NCRPO district directors
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Seven senior officials have been reassigned in the latest reorganization of the Philippine National Police (PNP), including the directors of two police districts in the National…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Seven senior officials have been reassigned in the latest reorganization of the Philippine National Police (PNP), including the directors of two police districts in the National Capital Region.

In a document obtained on Sunday, Eastern Police District (EPD) Director Brig. Gen. Melecio Buslig Jr. was designated as chief of the PNP Firearms and Explosives Office (FEO), while Southern Police District (SPD) Director Brig. Gen. Glenn Oliver Cinco was named chief of the Supervisory Office for Security and Investigation Agencies (SOSIA).
The FEO, a specialized unit under the PNP Civil Security Group (CSG), regulates and manages the legal ownership, control, and use of firearms and explosives in the country.
The SOSIA, also under the CSG, is responsible for regulating, licensing and supervising private security agencies.
Brig. Gen. Roman Arugay, formerly with the Office of the PNP chief, will take over as Buslig as EPD director, while Brig. Gen. Rodel Pastor will assume the post of SPD director from Cinco.
Meanwhile, Police Regional Office (PRO)-Eastern Visayas Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy was designated chief of the Human Rights Affairs Office, also under the Office of the PNP chief.
Capoy will be replaced by Brig. Gen. Romano Cardiño, who will pass the leadership of PRO-Negros Island Region to Brig. Gen. Rudecindo Reales.
The reshuffle takes effect Sept. 7.

articles.title: Jamaican delegates arrive in UK to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles
articles.summary:
Slavery’s legacy continues ‘to deprive our country and our people’, says minister, as group prepares to appeal to Jamaica’s head of state

A landmark petition is to be handed to King Charles…

blocks.text: A landmark petition is to be handed to King Charles by Jamaican over slavery reparations, aiming to confront historical crimes that still disadvantage former British colonies, the Caribbean nation’s culture minister has said.
The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.

“We’re a resilient people. We were able to bounce back from [Hurricane] Melissa, for example,” said Olivia Grange, who arrived in London at the weekend with members of Jamaica’s National Council on Reparations.
“But we still have a lot of work to do, and you can imagine if we did not have those inherited problems, the legacy that came out of slavery, how much better we would have been able to do so.”

First announced in June last year, the petition asks the monarch to use his authority to request legal advice from the judicial committee of the London-based privy council, the final court of appeal for UK overseas territories and some Commonwealth countries.

It wants Charles to ask whether the forced transport of Africans to Jamaica was lawful, if it constituted a crime against humanity, and whether Britain is under obligation to provide restitution to Jamaica for slavery and its enduring consequences.
Grange said that these questions and a privy council response were critical to progressing the country’s reparations claims.
Between the 15th and 19th centuries, more than 12.5 million Africans were kidnapped, forcibly transported to the Americas and sold into slavery.

Grange said that Jamaica had been the first Caribbean nation to create a national reparations mechanism, establishing it in 2009. She said the aim was to address the enduring impacts of slavery, that put countries such as Jamaica at a grave economic disadvantage and affected its ability to respond to modern-day challenges in the Caribbean, such as the climate crisis.

“We have inherited systems that continue to deprive our country and our people. The legacy in education, even in health, the way we eat, our diet because of what we were fed, our ancestors were fed,” she said.
Ralph Gonsalves, a former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines who was instrumental in setting up the Caribbean Community Reparations Commission, echoed Grange’s sentiments.

“The present is very much the past, because what we are dealing with is the legacies of underdevelopment which you can source, and we do source, to native genocide and enslavement of African bodies,” he said on Sunday.

“People must remember this: that European nations were enriched because of the enslavement of African bodies.” Gonsalves is an elder and adviser for the Repair Campaign, a social movement for reparatory justice.

He said Jamaica’s visit was a critical milestone among a number of upcoming events, including a Caribbean reparations conference in Barbados later this month, and planned advocacy at the upcoming UN general assembly in late September and the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua in November, which King Charles is scheduled to attend.
after newsletter promotion

There are growing global calls for Britain and other former colonial powers to recognise hundreds of years of transatlantic slavery that treated African people as chattel as a crime, and to engage in a process of reparatory justice.

In March this year, 123 nations voted for a landmark UN resolution that described chattel slavery as the gravest crime against humanity. In June, the Caribbean launched a manifesto outlining the “moral, ethical and legal case for reparations”. And last month, a UN committee on the elimination of racial discrimination said countries were legally obliged to consider reparations for the transatlantic slave trade and take other ⁠measures to address the enduring ⁠legacy of racial ​discrimination.

The UK was one of several European countries that abstained from voting in the March UN resolution, and in October 2024, the former British prime minister Keir Starmer resisted pressure from member states to include reparations in the Commonwealth heads of government meeting agenda.
Grange said she hoped the visit would facilitate a unifying response to the complicated history.

On Sunday, the delegation will host a remembrance church service in Brixton, and later in the week they are due to meet UK members of parliament. Grange said there would also be a visit to the British Museum, to discuss repatriation of Jamaican artefacts.

She said: “We may have different history, different heritage, different skin colour, but it’s about humanity. It’s about, as a people, being able to live together, to work together, and to respect each other.

“And in our efforts to seek reparatory justice, we will use the opportunity to also promote and encourage what Jamaica is known for, One Love, because we have the song of the century through Bob Marley.”

articles.title: U.S. envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Kyiv after talks with Putin in Moscow
articles.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday in their first official visit to Ukraine as part of a renewed push for peace more than four and a half years after Russia's…

image.caption: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, left, greets U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff prior to talks in Kyiv on Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026. (Efrem Lukatsky/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday in their first official visit to Ukraine as part of a renewed push for peace more than four and a half years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Saturday's meeting in Moscow ended without any major developments being announced
The trip by the Americans follows a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday, as both sides have engaged in escalating aerial attacks recently.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday that his government is ready for a "constructive" discussion with the U.S. emissaries.

"We are interested in bringing the end of the war closer. Peace is needed. Security guarantees are needed. A just and sustainable postwar peace is needed. Our proposals are prepared," Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram.
The envoys arrived by train and were welcomed at the station in Ukraine's capital by high-ranking Ukrainian officials, before being met by Zelenskyy at a ceremony in St. Sophia Square.

Washington's push to end the fighting has lost momentum, with the Trump administration focused for the past six months on the Iran war. The last known visit to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, was in January when they also held talks with Putin at the Kremlin.

items: Putin meets with U.S. envoys at the Kremlin in renewed talks over war in Ukraine

blocks.text: No breakthroughs in Moscow talks

Saturday's meeting in Moscow lasted more than three hours behind closed doors and ended without any major developments being announced. Putin's foreign policy adviser, Yuri Ushakov, described the talks as constructive, frank and useful, but he didn't discuss specific outcomes.
U.S. officials in Moscow with new proposal to end Russia-Ukraine war
While Moscow offered its "comprehensive assessment" of the battlefield situation in Ukraine, Ushakov said, the talks weren't purely focused on the war in Ukraine.
"Economic issues and potentially large, mutually beneficial joint projects for Russia and America were discussed in considerable detail," he said.
Russia and Ukraine continue to exchange fire

The air war between Russia and Ukraine has intensified as troops have struggled to make progress along the 1,250-kilometre front line. Russia has recently been using fast-flying, jet-powered drones, and the recurring wail of air-raid sirens has become part of daily life in Kyiv.
Putin and Zelenskyy had agreed to pause strikes on each other's capitals while the talks take place. Still, the two traded fire overnight into Sunday, officials said.
Russian attacks across multiple Ukrainian regions killed one person and wounded at least 10 others overnight into Sunday, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said.

items: Russian attack hits Ukraine's security service headquarters

blocks.text: In Zaporizhzhia, drone strikes killed a 74-year-old man and wounded three people, while a drone damaged an apartment building, wounding seven people, in the Khmelnytskyi region.
Ukraine's air force said Sunday that it intercepted 82 drones out of the 108 launched by Russia overnight, along with six missiles.
In Russia, a man was killed and a woman was seriously wounded when a Ukrainian drone struck a vehicle, according to local authorities in the Belgorod border region.

The Russian Defense Ministry said Sunday that its air defenses overnight shot down 258 Ukrainian drones over 14 Russian regions, the Russia-occupied Crimean Peninsula and the waters of the Black and Azov Seas.
Mixed hopes on the ground
In Kyiv on Sunday, dozens gathered for a nationwide 9 a.m. moment of silence honouring Ukraine's fallen soldiers, a daily ritual held in cities across the country.

Nataliia Lipei, 67, whose son Viktor was killed in December 2022, was among those who attended. Despite a health condition, she has travelled from city to city to take part, and said she hopes the talks in Moscow and Kyiv will finally bring an end to the war.

"I hope these steps and these meetings will definitely produce results, because there has been so much bloodshed and so many deaths here that we have to stop all of this," Lipei told The Associated Press.
Not everyone shared her hope for the talks. Oleksandr Pastukhov, a 27-year-old video editor who joined the commemoration, was skeptical that the envoys' visit would change anything.

"We've already seen delegations like this come here before," he said. "We've seen this so-called ceasefire for three days, which ended after just a couple of hours, and now we're supposed to naively think that two people will come and change something."

articles.title: Baguio sets Burnham Lake boat fare at P250
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY — The city government ordered Burnham Park boat concessionaires to retain the P250 rental fee for a 30-minute ride, regardless of boat size, following a reported rate increase after the…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — The city government ordered Burnham Park boat concessionaires to retain the P250 rental fee for a 30-minute ride, regardless of boat size, following a reported rate increase after the lake reopened.

The status quo took effect Sept. 2 after a meeting led by City Environment and Parks Management Office (CEPMO) head Rhenan Diwas, with City Administrator Vittorio Jerico Cawis also in attendance. Diwas said no rate increase had been authorized, as any adjustment still requires City Council approval.
Only two of the nine boat owners had complied with the city’s boat upgrading requirement as of Sept. 2, Diwas said. Boats that have not been upgraded will not be allowed for public use.

The concessionaires were also ordered to issue official receipts to customers. Diwas said an earlier agreement allowing a possible rental fee adjustment was conditional on compliance with the upgrading requirement and securing City Council approval.
Cawis warned that concessionaires who continue to disregard the requirements could lose their slots, which would then be opened to other interested residents. “This is the final warning,” he said.

The meeting followed Mayor Benjamin Magalong’s directive for an immediate investigation into the reported increase in boat rental fees. Magalong warned that concessionaires found taking advantage of the public would face sanctions.
The Burnham Park lake reopened on Sept. 1 after 10 months of rehabilitation as part of the city’s 117th Charter Day anniversary celebration. /mcm
