articles.title: Canadian skyrunner goes missing during training session for Matterhorn record attempt
articles.summary:
• Kalie McCrystal was hoping to break record in Alps

  • Athlete was last seen on Tuesday afternoon

Canadian athlete Kalie McCrystal has gone missing during…

blocks.text: Canadian athlete Kalie McCrystal has gone missing during preparations for a record attempt in the Alps.

McCrystal, from Squamish in British Columbia, was on a “reconnaissance/training session” in the run-up to her attempt at ascending and descending the 14,692 ft (4,478m) Matterhorn on the Swiss-Italian border.

According to the Skyrunner World Series, the 38-year-old was last seen on Tuesday after she had reached the Matterhorn’s summit and was descending the Italian side of the mountain. The last sighting of the athlete was near a shelter at an altitude of around 12,500 ft.
“There has been no further contact with her, and no one has seen or heard from her since,” the Skyrunner World Series said in the press release.
Skyrunning involves running and scrambling at altitudes higher than 6,600ft. McCrystal was hoping to ascend and descend the Matterhorn in less than five hours during her record attempt.
A helicopter search for McCrystal was called off on Friday after rescuers could find no trace of the athlete.
McCrystal has climbed the Matterhorn before and, according to the Skyrunner World Series, she had “many years of experience in high-altitude and technical mountain terrain”.
A friend of McCrystal said he did not believe the athlete had taken unnecessary risks before she went missing.

“I know that this objective was well within her capabilities,” Duncan O’Regan, McCrystal’s friend and fellow mountain runner, told CBC. “She’s done much more difficult things, and this is not something that is beyond her capabilities. She’s comfortable in this terrain.”
McCrystal has set several skyrunning records in Canada and Europe and is a lawyer and staff member at Capilano University in North Vancouver.

“Our thoughts are with Kalie’s family, friends and colleagues, and with everyone involved in the search efforts during this incredibly difficult time,” said Jason Dewling, the university’s president and vice-chancellor.

articles.title: Trump envoys arrive in Kyiv for first Ukraine visit
articles.summary: KYIV, Ukraine — US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Kyiv Sunday for their first visit to the Ukrainian capital, a day after holding talks with Russia’s Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin…

blocks.text: KYIV, Ukraine — US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Kyiv Sunday for their first visit to the Ukrainian capital, a day after holding talks with Russia’s Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on ending more than four years of war between the neighbors.
US President Donald Trump’s business partner Witkoff and son-in-law Kushner had visited Moscow several times but had not held talks in Kyiv, which has been hit by deadly Russian strikes since 2022.
They are due to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. An AFP reporter in Kyiv saw the American envoys arrive by train.
They are hoping to revive negotiations to end Europe’s worst conflict since World War II, after a summer of escalation.
Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
Witkoff and Kushner met with Putin on Saturday to “advance President Trump’s agenda of peace in the Russia-Ukraine War,” a White House official said in a statement to AFP.
“The two sides discussed substantive plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks, and look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow in Ukraine.”
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov called the talks “extremely frank,” saying the Americans “put forward a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement,” but did not elaborate.
The Russian side told the Americans that Moscow was “confident” it could achieve its military goals of seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine, Ushakov added.
Both Russia and Ukraine have vowed not to strike each other’s capitals for three days to allow the negotiations to take place.
It was Kushner and Witkoff’s eighth visit to Moscow during the war, but it is their first in the Ukrainian capital, which has been hit by deadly Russian strikes throughout the war.
Russia’s TASS news agency reported early Sunday that Witkoff and Kushner had arrived in Rzeszow, Poland, on their way to Kyiv.
Zelensky on Sunday said Ukraine was “ready for the conversation.”
“Ukraine has always been and will remain constructive,” the wartime leader said on social media ahead of their visit.
The country’s airspace has been closed since Moscow launched the war in February 2022, and visiting leaders have been arriving by train.
For many Ukrainians, hopes of a breakthrough remain slim.
“At this point it doesn’t give me any hope. There have already been too many negotiations,” Yaroslav, a 29-year-old Kyiv resident, told AFP.
Putin thanks Trump
In televised comments before the talks, Putin said Russia would ensure the safety of the envoys in Kyiv, a city Moscow has pounded with deadly strikes throughout the war.
“We will do everything that depends on us to ensure the safety of the negotiation process and mediators such as yourselves,” Putin told Witkoff and Kushner.
Earlier Saturday, Putin had thanked Trump for persisting in his efforts to end the war despite it being “not simple.”
Of the envoys’ trip to Kyiv, he said: “No matter what happens next, contacts of this kind are undoubtedly always beneficial.”
Trump said on Friday his envoys were bringing a “proposal” to end the fighting.
“We have an idea for peace,” he said, without elaborating.
US efforts have so far not led to a breakthrough in the war, and peace efforts have stalled in part because of Washington’s war with Iran.
Russia occupied large swaths of eastern and southern Ukraine, and Putin has insisted Moscow is intent on seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine.
Limited truce
Both Moscow and Kyiv committed to suspending strikes as the negotiations took place.
“The Russian president, the commander in chief, has given the order from midnight not to strike Kyiv for three days,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
Zelensky said he had spoken to the US envoys and also promised Kyiv would not strike Moscow.
“From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow,” Zelensky said.
But fighting continued elsewhere. Ukraine’s air force said Russia attacked overnight with 108 drones and missiles, while Moscow said it had shot down 258 drones.
On Saturday, Putin said he had “noted that the Ukrainian side significantly reduced” its strikes on Russia and Moscow.
However, Kyiv said that Russian strikes had killed 10 people across the country on Saturday, including a child and his family members in the Kharkiv region and two people outside Kyiv. /mcm

articles.title: Indonesia’s main airport suspends operations after volcanic eruption
articles.summary: JAKARTA, Indonesia — Indonesia halted operations at its main international airport outside Jakarta on Sunday after ash spewed from the Anak Krakatoa volcano more than 150 kilometers away, impacting…

blocks.text: JAKARTA, Indonesia — Indonesia halted operations at its main international airport outside Jakarta on Sunday after ash spewed from the Anak Krakatoa volcano more than 150 kilometers away, impacting thousands of passengers.
Mount Anak Krakatoa erupted on Saturday, producing a fountain of lava and booming sounds that could be heard up to a few hundred kilometers away, the geology agency said in a statement.
Two new eruptions were recorded on Sunday, the volcanology agency warned.

Ash from the volcano was detected in the airspace surrounding Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, prompting authorities to initially suspend operations from 1:30 a.m. Sunday (Saturday 1830 GMT) to 5:30 a.m.
The suspension was extended three times, with the latest ending at 5:30 p.m. Sunday “due to increased eruptive activity,” the airport said in a social media post.

Operations have been suspended at six airports, including Husein Sastranegara Airport in Bandung and Radin Inten II Airport near Bandar Lampung on Sumatra, the country’s Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said.
Several airports in cities, including Semarang and Surabaya, have been prepared as “alternatives for landing,” Dudy added.
Passengers scrambling
The disruption left some passengers scrambling to find alternative flights.
Henny Yensan, 44, who had hoped to go back to her hometown with her mother, said “everybody was disappointed.”
“No one flew into a rage, because after all, this is due to a natural disaster,” the businesswoman, who had to reschedule her flight to Tuesday, told AFP.
Samuel Guiberteau, a Danone executive on a business trip to Lombok since Friday, said “nothing is certain for the moment,” as he searched for alternative flights back to the capital.
“I had found another flight on Citilink, but it was also canceled,” the 47-year-old told AFP by phone, adding that he had no alternative but to stay in Lombok for the time being.
More than 22,000 passengers have been impacted by the suspension, the Transportation Ministry said, adding that 209 flights were affected, in particular those to and from Singapore.
Other affected international routes included Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur.
At least 16 domestic flights to and from Bali were also canceled, local airport authorities said.
Hazard warning
Anak Krakatoa, which means Child of Krakatoa, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
Ships passing through the strait were asked to increase vigilance for possible disruption to navigation safety due to volcanic activity.
Vessels are prohibited from approaching the exclusion zone within a three-kilometer radius of the volcano, local port authorities said in a statement.
The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of the last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatoa.
That disaster was one of the deadliest and most destructive in history, with an estimated 35,000 people killed.
Geology agency head Lana Saria said “seismic activity indicates the movement or release of volcanic fluids within the volcanic system.”
“However, the timing, magnitude and nature of the next eruption cannot be precisely predicted,” Lana added.
Lana warned against approaching Anak Krakatoa, saying materials ejected from the volcano could endanger those within the exclusion zone.
She said the most recent series of eruptions does not have the potential to trigger a tsunami at this time.
A 2018 tsunami, triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatoa, killed 429 people and left thousands displaced.
Indonesia, a Southeast Asian archipelago nation, sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where the meeting of continental plates causes high volcanic and seismic activity.

articles.title: 'Never experienced anything to this size and effect,' official says of Cape Breton storm
articles.summary: The CAO for Port Hawkesbury, N.S., says the damage from a torrential downpour that saw more than 200 millimetres of rain dumped on parts of Cape Breton is unlike anything he's seen before.

image.caption: Waves from the Bras d'Or Lake batter West Bay Road in Dundee, washing storm debris across the asphalt. (Tom Ayers/CBC)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·Updated
The CAO for Port Hawkesbury, N.S., says the damage from a torrential downpour that saw more than 200 millimetres of rain dumped on parts of Cape Breton is unlike anything he's seen before.
Environment Canada says parts of the island could see 10 to 20 millimetres more rain
· CBC News
· Posted: Sep 06, 2026 7:49 AM EDT | Last Updated: 10 minutes ago
"We've never experienced anything to this size and effect," said Terry Doyle. "And certainly, that's what I'm being told by others as well."

Doyle spoke Sunday from an emergency response co-ordination centre where representatives from Victoria, Inverness and Richmond counties and the province are gathered. A state of emergency was declared Saturday for those three counties.
Doyle said the bulk of the damage is in Richmond County, around the Bras d'Or Lake, with a significant number of roads, bridges and driveways that are washed out.
Doyle and other municipal officials are asking people to stay at home to allow crews to repair roads.
Inverness County Warden Bonny MacIsaac said many roads are washed out and a lot of trees have fallen in her area.

"There was a lot of floodwaters. Nobody wants to run into anything like that. And we're asking [people] not to drive through flooded roads. You might not see that the road is unstable underneath that," she said Sunday morning.
If people must travel, she said they should check 511, the provincial website providing road conditions, before going out.
The damage from the rainfall includes flooding, power outages and washed-out roads.

items: Mobile readers conserving data can see the CBC Lite version of this story here

blocks.text: Amanda Mombourquette, councillor for Richmond County District 4, said some residents are stranded due to road closures.

"[We're] very concerned about folks who may be in vulnerable situations who are now stranded from access to things like emergency services or the basics of going to get groceries, that kind of thing," she said.

items: State of emergency declared in 3 Cape Breton counties after storm, flooding

blocks.text: Rainfall warnings are in effect for Victoria and Cape Breton counties, as well as Sydney. Environment Canada says 10 to 20 millimetres of rain are expected from today until Monday morning, with higher amounts possible in some areas.
As of 8:30 a.m. AT Sunday, Nova Scotia Power's outage map shows that more than 5,000 customers province-wide are without power, mostly in Chéticamp.
Coun. Claude Poirier, who represents Chéticamp on Inverness County council, said most of the community is without power.
He said he wasn't aware of local storm damage or road closures because of the storm.
Poirier said the local Legion and fire department have opened up comfort centres so people can charge their devices or have a hot cup of coffee or tea.
Municipalities in Cape Breton opened a toll-free support line Sunday — 902-625-7888 — where residents can report non-emergency issues and concerns.

articles.title: US envoys Kushner and Witkoff arrive in Kyiv to hold talks on ending war
articles.summary:
Arrival marks the pair’s first visit to Ukraine and comes day after ‘substantive plans’ were discussed in Moscow

The US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Kyiv for a…

blocks.text: The US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Kyiv for a second day of talks on how to end the war in Ukraine.

Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, met Kushner and Witkoff in Sophia Square, in front of Kyiv’s historic Saint Sophia Cathedral. Zelenskyy greeted Witkoff with a hug, saying: “It’s good to see you, Steve.”

The cathedral is a few hundred metres away from the headquarters of Ukraine’s intelligence services, which was hit by a Russian drone on Friday afternoon, marking an escalation in a conflict that has now dragged on for more than four years.

blocks.caption: The trio met in Kyiv’s Sophia Square. Photograph: Efrem Lukatsky/AP

blocks.text: Witkoff and Kushner are meeting with Ukraine’s president the day after holding three hours of talks in Moscow with Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin.

The US envoys have visited Russia several times, but this is their first visit to Ukraine. The trip is intended to mark an intensification of efforts to end the war in Ukraine, although details of any peace proposal remain unclear.
British, French ⁠and ⁠German national security ​advisers were reportedly in ⁠Kyiv on Sunday before Witkoff and Kushner’s ‌arrival.

Talks between Russia and Ukraine on ending the war have focused on a 20-point peace plan put forward by Washington and Kyiv in December. But the two sides have failed to reach common ground on several sticking points, including control of territory in the east of the country.
A White House official said on Saturday that the talks with Moscow “discussed substantive plans for next steps” for ending the war and said that an announcement would follow in “coming weeks”.
The senior Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the talks as “extremely frank” and said there was an acknowledgement of the need to address “the root causes of the conflict”.

blocks.caption: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held talks with Vladimir Putin, right, in Moscow on Saturday. Photograph: Mikhail Metzel/Reuters

blocks.text: Moscow and Kyiv pledged to refrain from strikes on each other’s capital cities for three days to ensure the smooth passage of the negotiators. Zelenskyy said on Sunday that the plans for the US envoys to fly into Moscow had been upended by Russian strikes on Kyiv’s two main airports on Friday evening.
Ukraine’s airspace has been closed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Other visiting dignitaries have travelled overland by train from neighbouring countries.
Kyiv and the surrounding areas have been hit by a barrage of daily drone attacks for more than a week, the most sustained attack on Ukraine’s capital in months.
after newsletter promotion

The capital is now enjoying a reprieve from strikes and air raid alerts that had become a daily occurrence, but other parts of the country are still being hit. Ukrainian authorities reported on Sunday that at least eight people were killed and 69 injured across Ukraine in the past day.

Ukraine is facing a critical shortage of US-made Patriot interceptors which can shoot down incoming threats. Many of the recent Russian strikes have been by new-model jet-powered drones that can reach speeds of 250mph, making them hard to intercept.

Many Ukrainians are worried about the war dragging on into a fifth year and are anxious about the winter ahead. This week, Zelenskyy’s defence technology adviser, Serhii Beskrestnov, told the Guardian that the government should consider evacuating elderly people from the capital as Putin has ordered his military to “prepare and carry out mass strikes” on Ukraine’s energy facilities.
Russia and Ukraine have increased their use of long-range missiles in recent weeks in an effort to grind down morale in each other’s countries.
Additional research by Illia Dyadik

articles.title: Butuan declares state of calamity as water crisis worsens
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Butuan City has been placed under a state of calamity as a prolonged extreme dry spell continues to disrupt water services, affecting a third of its population. The…

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Butuan City has been placed under a state of calamity as a prolonged extreme dry spell continues to disrupt water services, affecting a third of its population.
The state of calamity was declared on Saturday, Sept. 5, during the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) 3rd Special Session, which was presided over by Vice Mayor Reynante Desiata.
“The resolution was approved as the continuing water shortage has significantly affected residents’ access to water across several barangays,” the SP said in a statement.

As of Sept. 4, the Butuan City Water District (BCWD) reported that 91,425, or a third of its 269,000 residents, are experiencing low-pressure to no-water service as water availability continues to decline.
The water shortage is linked to the prevailing dry spell in Agusan del Norte, including Butuan City, which has experienced a significant rainfall deficit.
The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration said the province had been under dry spell conditions since Aug. 23.

BCWD and the city government have already implemented water rationing and other measures in affected areas, but these interventions remain insufficient as the shortage continues, the resolution stated.

While residents acknowledged the importance of water rationing during emergencies, a constituent pointed out that the program should not become a substitute for reliable infrastructure and long-term preparation.
“Emergency measures should remain emergency measures. They cannot become institutionalized substitutes for infrastructure,” Luna Kaisog stated.

The state of calamity declaration allows the city government and affected barangays to mobilize additional resources and access their quick response funds for measures such as the supply and installation of water tanks, tankers, pumps, filtration systems, and other needs for water distribution and rationing.
The city Public Information Office (PIO) said the local government is doing everything possible to assist affected residents.

Authorities are assessing several pumping stations for possible rehabilitation. Based on BCWD recommendations, Pumping Stations 2, 3, and 16 have been identified as potential sources of additional water.

The city government and BCWD are also considering conducting geo-resistivity surveys to locate groundwater sources, assess aquifer levels, and determine whether the water found is fresh or saline. Several areas are also being evaluated for possible re-drilling.
The PIO said any source considered for rehabilitation or development would undergo testing to determine its water quality, yield, and long-term reliability before being used for public distribution.
An open letter from concerned residents questioned the reliability of the BCWD’s water sources, its contingency measures, and the billing of customers who receive little or no water.
Engr. Sergio Pascual, a former city councilor, blamed the crisis on what he described as an alleged failure of leadership among city officials.
Pascual said water shortages had been a recurring problem for about a decade, yet the city government had failed, according to him, to establish a long-term solution. /mcm

articles.title: NLEX, MMDA complete flood-defense works in San Simon
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The flood-defense works on the San Simon stretch of North Luzon Expressway in Pampanga have been completed with the help of the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA),…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The flood-defense works on the San Simon stretch of North Luzon Expressway in Pampanga have been completed with the help of the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), the NLEX Corp. said on Sunday.
The works cover the following:

items: shoulder impounding and lining at San Simon and Tulaoc
continuous flood barrier lines along the affected stretch
a combined fleet of high-capacity pumps

blocks.text: NLEX noted that the MMDA sent equipment outside its home jurisdiction to Pampanga, with its crews working alongside NLEX teams to do the following:

items: Position a pump unit at the Kilometer 56 marker, with its suction line running over the guardrail to draw floodwater off the carriageway.
Install L-type interlocking flood barriers, ballasted and backed with sandbags and modular mesh-and-liner barrier units to form a continuous line along the affected shoulder.

blocks.caption: An MMDA pump at the Kilometer 56 marker on NLEX. —Photo from NLEX

blocks.text: MMDA dump trucks hauled barrier sections, sandbags, and fill to the worksite, carrying out the work ahead of the southwest monsoon onslaught.
The barrier line was reinforced rapidly when the rivers overflowed, a sequence documented in a timestamped photographic record through Aug. 31.

blocks.caption: Reinforcing the flood barrier at the San Simon stretch of NLEX on Aug. 31, 2026. —Photo from NLEX

blocks.text: Standing arrangement
“We are grateful to the MMDA for going beyond its own jurisdiction to stand with us here,” said Luis S. Reñon, NLEX Corp. president and general manager.

“Their pumping units, their barriers, and their people were in the water with our teams, and that partnership is the reason this stretch is defended today. What the two agencies built together in a week, we intend to keep.”

After the late-August flooding, NLEX rented additional heavy-duty pumps beyond its own fleet when it exceeded the capacity of company-owned equipment, impounded and lined the shoulders at San Simon and Tulaoc so that water would be held and channeled away from live lanes, and had response crews prepositioned at Meycauayan, Paso de Blas, San Fernando, and Balintawak.
NLEX and MMDA now follow a written protocol assigning pumping responsibility, lane-closure authority, and public advisory duties.
“The work on this stretch of the expressway continues,” Reñon said.
“Equipment and personnel remain in place, and NLEX and the MMDA will keep reinforcing it through the season. Motorists can expect the road to be prepared before conditions change.”

blocks.caption: MMDA trucks hauling materials for the flood barrier at the San Simon stretch of NLEX. —Photo from NLEX

blocks.text: Heavy traffic due to flooding

On Aug. 29, a dike gave way northeast of the San Simon interchange, and floodwater from the town crossed overland onto the carriageway, closing lanes between Pulilan and San Fernando and causing heavy traffic.
San Simon has no prior record of flooding, and no waterway runs from the dike to the expressway. The arrangement between the MMDA and NLEX, assembled during the event, has since continued.
“Motorists were stranded on that stretch, so we sent our pumps, our barriers and our personnel,” MMDA General Manager Nicolas Torre III said.
“Our crews worked in the water beside NLEX’s, and the equipment stays for as long as this stretch needs it. We will keep working with NLEX to keep that road open and passable.”

Longer-term measures for the stretch are under study, among them sheet piling along the exposed section, sustained high-capacity pumping, and deepening of the Tulaoc River to increase discharge capacity.

For motorists, toll relief on the Pulilan–San Fernando stretch has been in effect since noon on Sept. 2. It will remain in place until all lanes are passable to all vehicle classes, with rebates of ₱113 for Class 1, ₱281 for Class 2, and ₱338 for Class 3 credited to RFID accounts the day after passage.
Advisories will be issued through NLEX channels, roadside signage, and broadcast partners before any lane closure. /atm

articles.title: Farage says overseas donation row ‘looks bad’ but denies Reform breached electoral law
articles.summary:
Robert Jenrick says party has followed legal protocol ‘at all times’ as Met police consider launching investigation

Nigel Farage has acknowledged the overseas donation row engulfing Reform…

blocks.text: Nigel Farage has acknowledged the overseas donation row engulfing Reform UK “looks bad” for his party but denied it had ever taken foreign money in breach of electoral law.

The Reform leader, who is battling to contain the fallout from the allegations, was asked to categorically rule out that foreign money had ever been funnelled to his party. He replied: “I can … never happened.”

Farage was forced to suspend his close aide Dan Jukes and Reform’s head of policy, James Orr, on Friday after they were filmed in an undercover investigation apparently plotting to get around electoral laws on foreign donations.

In an interview with the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg, Farage described their comments as “injudicious at best” and admitted the optics of the undercover filming were problematic for his party, which has in the past tried to suggest it would do politics differently.
“This looks bad, as does the sale of peerages, as does government contracts for donations,” he said. “We are not the first people to be involved in a row over donations.”

The Metropolitan police are now assessing the evidence after a complaint that Farage and his aides have broken political funding laws, with sources suggesting a full investigation is expected to be launched. They all deny wrongdoing.
Scotland Yard could extend an existing investigation into whether Reform took donations channelled through an intermediary from potentially impermissible sources, which the party and donors deny.

Farage is already facing intense scrutiny about Reform’s finances, as well as a £5m gift by a crypto billionaire shortly before announcing he would stand in the 2024 general election, which he has since said was intended to pay for security.

In an earlier extract of the BBC interview, Farage also claimed he “wasn’t even listening” during the meeting at the centre of the controversy, and that he knew donation law “better than anybody”, as he sought to limit the damage caused by the allegations.

Robert Jenrick, Reform’s Treasury spokesperson, said on Sunday that he had seen legal advice that the party had not in fact broken electoral law over foreign donations but that lessons would be learned from the episode.

blocks.caption: Reform MP Robert Jenrick has said a KC reviewed the evidence and found the party had not broken any laws. Photograph: Temilade Adelaja/Reuters

blocks.text: “We’re going to investigate exactly what happened,” Jenrick told Sky News. “It’s right to have due process. But this is not the way that Reform conducts itself.
after newsletter promotion

“Like any political party, we seek to abide by the law at all times, and we believe we have in this case. In fact, I’ve reviewed the legal advice from the KC who’s advised the party in the last 48 hours, and it shows that, yeah, we did.
“But do we want for the best version of ourselves? Yes, absolutely. And no doubt there will be lessons to be learnt from this.”

Speaking after the BBC interview, the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said: “For a political party that don’t like foreigners much they do seem to have a soft spot for foreign cash. We have rules in this country about how our democracy works and everyone has to stick to them.”
He added: “I think you see someone struggling to decide whether they’re really serious about trying to run for power or want to keep the protest going.”

articles.title: Gilas Pilipinas suffers back-to-back blowouts to Korea ahead of Asian Games
articles.summary: Gilas Pilipinas fails to win either of its two tuneup games against South Korea — losses that underscore the daunting task of defending its Asian Games throne

blocks.text: DRIVE. Gilas Pilipinas' Sedrick Barefield and South Korea's Lee Hyun-jung during their tune-up game in Suwon, South Korea, on September 6, 2026.
Korea Basketball Association
Gilas Pilipinas fails to win either of its two tuneup games against South Korea — losses that underscore the daunting task of defending its Asian Games throne

MANILA, Philippines – Another slow start doomed Gilas Pilipinas as it absorbed a second straight loss to host South Korea, 69-42, to close out the Hana Bank Invitational in Suwon on Sunday, September 6.

The Nationals managed just four points in the opening quarter and never came within striking distance the rest of the way, failing to win either of their two tuneup games against the Koreans just days before opening their Asian Games campaign in Nagoya, Japan.

Sedrick Barefield put the Philippines on the board first with a midrange jumper before Korea unleashed a 19-0 run that set the tone for the blowout, mirroring its 81-55 rout of the same opponents two days earlier.
Led by Yu Ki-sang and Yeo Jun-seok, Korea enjoyed a lead as big as 37 points midway through the third quarter, 53-16, as it coasted to the breezy triumph.

Yu fired a game-high 15 points on a 5-of-8 clip from three-point land, Yeo finished with 14 points and 5 rebounds, while Lee Hyun-jung turned in an all-around outing of 11 points, 15 rebounds, 6 assists, and 2 steals.
Zavier Lucero paced the Philippines with 14 points, 6 rebounds, and 3 assists, but lacked sufficient help as no other Filipino player scored in double figures.

Adrian Nocum finished with 9 points and 3 assists, while Sedrick Barefield and Brandon Ganuelas-Rosser chipped in 7 points apiece in a defeat that underscored the Filipinos’ daunting task of defending their Asian Games crown.
With only 11 players in the lineup, Gilas Pilipinas has its fingers crossed that Justin Brownlee, the hero of the 2023 championship squad, will make it to the quadrennial showpiece.
From Korea, the Nationals will fly to Japan for the Asian Games, where the men’s basketball tournament runs from September 10 to 20.
Bunched in Group C, the Philippines will open the Asian Games against Bahrain on September 11, then tangle with Kazakhstan and China on September 12 and 14, respectively. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Black-clad Dover protesters condemned for ‘dressing up in costumes’ by minister
articles.summary:
Business secretary says masked anti-immigration protest was ‘not something we would want’ on British streets

A cabinet minister has condemned the blocking of Dover roads by dozens of masked…

blocks.text: A cabinet minister has condemned the blocking of Dover roads by dozens of masked and black-clad people on Saturday.

Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, said that although peaceful protest was an “essential part of British life”, this differed from “dressing up in costumes like this and disrupting people’s lives”.
He told the Sky News Sunday Morning programme: “So I would condemn it, but I’d condemn the disruption it caused for local people as well.”
Adding that the situation had been resolved, he said: “Clearly, that’s not something we would want or expect to see on the [streets] of Britain.”

He declined to comment “on the security and policing side of it”, but when pressed on the apparent unpreparedness of the police, he said he thought that “on the whole, the police handled it very well”.

Responsibility for the demonstration appears to have been claimed by Patriot Platform, an anti-immigration group with links to the far right which styles itself as having a “fierce love for our homeland”.

Kent police attended and engaged with the protest on Saturday, which the Port of Dover described as a “public order incident”. Protesters had dispersed by lunchtime, and no arrests were made during the incident.

Traffic in and out of the port on the A20 was stopped, causing delays of up to 45 minutes and four miles of congestion, according to National Highways. Videos shared online showed masked people in black marching on the road in a group as lorries waited in traffic next to police cars. The number of people involved was not immediately clear, and police did not give an official estimate. One livestreamer estimated that he was marching with hundreds of people.
Social media videos showed demonstrators linking arms in a blockade across the A20, chanting “stop the boats” and “England till I die”.
Mike Tapp, the Labour MP for Dover and Deal, posted on X: “A clearly coordinated protest is not ‘spontaneous’ as described by Police. We can and must do better.”
He noted that Kent police appeared to have had “little advance warning”, and questioned whether intelligence had been missed. “I will be asking why,” he wrote.
“Concerns around illegal migration are not racist. I’ve said that many times. But what we saw today in Dover is against our laws and not fair on residents.”
In a piece for the Mirror, Tapp suggested that he would like additional officers, including mutual aid from forces such as the Met, mobilised quickly if Dover is targeted again.

He wrote: “The Port of Dover is not just another road junction. It is critical national infrastructure, handling around a third of UK trade in goods with the EU and huge volumes of roll-on, roll-off freight. When Dover stops, Britain feels it.

“And the law matters. Wilfully obstructing a highway can be a criminal offence. New legislation also means police can designate protest areas where concealing your identity with a balaclava or other face covering becomes an offence.”
A government spokesperson said: “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but we condemn the behaviour in Dover and the travel disruption it has caused.”

articles.title: Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
articles.summary: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease…

image.caption: The Hyalomma tick prefers warm, dry conditions and, thanks to climate change, it is increasingly finding these further northImage: Fabian Sommer/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: It can spot its prey from up to 200 meters (about 650 feet) away — but unlike many of its fellow species, it doesn't lurk in the grass waiting for its victim to come closer. Instead it runs after it, chasing animals and humans alike.

The Hyalomma tick, often called "the great hunting tick," was previously found mostly in Africa, Asia, and southern Europe. But climate change means it can now survive further north and it has already been spotted in Germany and various Eastern European countries. Kosovo, in southeastern Europe, has been a hot spot for the tick for some time now.

The Hyalomma tick is also a vector of the highly pathogenic virus for Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, a potentially deadly disease with a high fatality rate. Symptoms of the disease are comparable to those of Ebola fever or the Marburg virus. These are capable of destroying blood and lymphatic vessels, which can lead to internal bleeding and death.
Ticks are spreading

Kurtesh Sherifi first read about Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever in the newspaper in 2005, when he was completing his studies as a veterinarian in Berlin. The article said that 11 people in his homeland, Kosovo, had contracted the disease and five had died. He was already interested in pathogens that can be transmitted between animals and humans, known as zoonoses, and Crimean-Congo fever intrigued him.

Back home, Sherifi started work with the faculty of agriculture and veterinary medicine at the University of Pristina. But the budget for research was tight. Kosovo, a small country with only about 1.6 million citizens, didn't have a high-security laboratory or the equipment necessary for investigating the Crimean-Congo fever virus.
Seeking German cooperation
Sherifi got in touch with Germany's largest institution for study in this area, the Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine in Hamburg.

One of the researchers was Petra Emmerich, a virologist and expert on what are known as Risk Group 4 viruses — viruses that cause severe, often fatal, diseases and usually have no widely available treatment. The Crimean-Congo virus is in that risk group.

Emmerich also acts as a reservist in the German military, which is especially interested in viruses that could be used as biological weapons. She was sent to Kosovo in 2009, which is when she met Sherifi.

blocks.caption: While the much smaller common longhorn beetle (left) waits for a suitable victim to pass by, the Hyalomma tick prefers to go huntingImage: Fabian Sommer/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A lively exchange began between the researchers. In Kosovo, a structure was established to monitor the spread of the Hyalomma tick and the virus. In 2013, the researchers' joint work began to receive funding through the German Biosecurity Program, run by the country's Foreign Ministry and "intended to help partner countries tackle biological threats."

"It's give and take," said Emmerich of the scientific partnership. "We have the diagnostic expertise and the necessary resources but we don't have the patients." Doctors from Germany regularly come to Kosovo with Emmerich where they can exchange information with their counterparts there.
Raising public awareness is another important pillar of the Germany-Kosovo cooperation.

Farmers in Kosovo are particularly susceptible to infection — and not solely due to ticks biting them, but because they often use their bare hands to remove ticks from animals. If infected blood from the animals gets into a small wound on the human hand, the virus can be transmitted to the human.
"This is quite likely how a large proportion of the [infected] population in Kosovo got infected," Sherifi explained.
Patients require intensive care, isolation
He and Emmerich have visited schools to educate students about the dangers of the virus and how to protect against it. For example, certain tick repellents help, as do long pants and sturdy shoes.

Not all Hyalomma ticks carry the virus, and most people who are bitten by a Hyalomma tick do not become ill. However, the larger problem is that there is neither a vaccine nor any specific course of treatment for those who do end up suffering from Crimean-Congo fever.

blocks.caption: Farmers in Kosovo are at particular risk from the Hyalomma ticksImage: Idro Seferi

blocks.text: "If you do get sick, it's particularly severe," Emmerich explained. The disease begins with nonspecific, flu-like symptoms including fever, chills, aches and headaches. In severe cases, a patient will begin bleeding from the skin, nose and gums and may also experience gastrointestinal bleeding. The worst causes can result in organ failure.
Patients require intensive care and isolation because they are highly contagious.

Much of the treatment in intensive care focuses on maintaining a patient's vital functions, but they are also given the antiviral drug, ribavirin. But, as Emmerich said, "ribavirin is not all that effective in acutely ill patients." That is something the scientists have seen firsthand with cases in Kosovo.

The best answer is prevention, which is why it's also very important for the researchers to monitor the spread of the Hyalomma ticks and for them to recommend avoiding certain areas where the ticks are prevalent, if possible.
Successful tick tactics

Over the years, the researchers have not only collected thousands of the ticks but they have also conducted so-called seroprevalence studies. These use blood tests to find antibodies from past infections. This allows the scientists to determine whether humans or animals have come in contact with the virus.

Farm animals are particularly suitable for this type of study, Sherifi said, as the virus doesn't affect them. And unlike wild animals and humans, they usually remain in a clearly defined area. That means that if antibodies are detected in the blood of these animals, it's clear the virus is circulating in that area.

In Kosovo, the number of serious infections has dropped drastically in the past decade, amounting to just five cases in total. In the previous decade, there were about 100 cases. Sherifi and Emmerich believe this indicates how successful their work has been.
Of course, that doesn't mean the ticks and the virus won't spread further in Europe, and the researchers both expect this to happen.
Hyalomma ticks with the Crimean-Congo virus have just been detected in France although, so far, no humans have been infected there.
"Over the past 13 years, Hyalomma ticks have spread geographically," said Emmerich. "As a virologist, that's something to think about, and it needs to be closely monitored."

This is why it's important for the German and Kosovar scientists to pass on what they've learned to countries that haven't yet had as much experience monitoring the Hyalomma ticks, such as Macedonia and Albania.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Germany plans anti-drone shield over Leipzig attack — report
articles.summary: Several German cities will receive rapidly deployable units capable of defending against drone strikes on critical infrastructure, according to Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

image.caption: Germany reportedly plans a new shield against sabotage at critical sitesImage: Ardan Fuessmann/IMAGO

blocks.text: Germany is planning a comprehensive protective shield to prevent attacks like the failed assault on Leipzig airport, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Sunday.
On August 4, several small drones targeted Leipzig-Halle Airport in eastern Germany, with one hitting a parked plane, while another is thought to have struck an inbound cargo jet.
German intelligence agencies blamed Russia for the incident, which Moscow has denied.

blocks.caption: Leipzig-Halle Airport is a major cargo hub used to fly weapons and supplies toward UkraineImage: Daniel Kessler/imageBROKER/picture alliance

blocks.text: What did Dobrindt say about the shield?
Dobrindt told Bild am Sonntag newspaper that Russia's hybrid attacks are now a "daily" reality, adding: "These attacks will increase, but we can defend ourselves and protect ourselves."
The newspaper cited information from the Interior Ministry showing the government plans to expand the federal police's mobile drone-defense units.
The measures include vehicles and helicopters that can be quickly deployed to protect airspace over key cities like Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin to counter drone attacks.
Bild said the shield would not only intercept drones, but could also defuse drone bombs and other explosive devices.
The newspaper described how a change in the law would allow critical infrastructure operators — including water, power and defense companies — to detect and defend against drone sabotage.

blocks.caption: Jammers flood drones with radio noise, so its pilot can no longer steer itImage: Michael Bihlmayer/Bihlmayerfotografie/IMAGO

blocks.text: Russia's Lavrov accuses Merz of wanting war
On Sunday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov claimed the German accusations levelled against Russia were "by ​and ​large, the ​start of ‌a real war."

He reiterated Russia's denial of any involvement with the Leipzig drone attack and criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz for wanting to boost the country's military capability in response to hybrid threats.

"All ‌these statements by Merz about making Germany the leading military power in ‌Europe once again — they are ‌being ​put into practice. He is, in effect, declaring war on us," Lavrov told Russian state-run TV channel Vesti.
He also criticized Germany's closure of Russian House cultural center in berlin and the Russian consulate in Bonn.
Putin denies Russian involvement in Leipzig drone attack
New tech planned to boost cyber security
Bild also described how a national protective cyber shield would be set up to detect and intercept hacking attacks.
The measure comes amid hundreds of cyberattacks on government departments, infrastructure and companies each day, many of them blamed on Russia, other states and criminal gangs.

The newspaper said the government ⁠also wants to increase the use of AI, biometric facial recognition ⁠and video surveillance, especially at transport hubs, to identify suspected attackers before they carry out attacks.
Over 1,000 drone sightings in 2025
The head of Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA), Holger Münch, told Bild in December that more than a thousand suspicious drone flights were recorded over Germany last year.
These incidents mostly targeted military sites, airports, ports and defense firms and were treated as surveillance or harassment, rather than attacks.
Leipzig airport has been targeted by sabotage before. In July 2024, a suspected Russian incendiary parcel caught fire at the airport's DHL hub.
The cargo hub is also utilized by the Ukrainian military and NATO to airlift arms for use in the Ukrainian defense against Russia's invasion.

articles.title: Zia Yusuf’s post about Camden council leader is ‘straightforward racism’, says minister
articles.summary:
Reform UK’s home affairs spokesperson has faced criticism within party after post about Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee

Labour has accused Reform’s Zia Yusuf of “straightforward…

blocks.text: Labour has accused Reform’s Zia Yusuf of “straightforward racism” after he suggested the party’s frontrunner to replace Keir Starmer in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection was not British.

Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee from Somalia and the leader of Camden council, has been tipped as an early favourite to contest the London seat for Labour after the former prime minister’s resignation.

Yusuf, Reform UK’s home affairs spokesperson, posted on X last week: “The frontrunner being foisted on the people of Holborn by Labour to replace the former prime minister Keir Starmer in our parliament was born in Somalia. Do you understand what’s happening?”

The post, which has been viewed 8m times, drew sharp criticism from several senior Reform UK figures during the party’s conference in Birmingham at the weekend. Appearing on Sky News on Sunday, the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, also condemned Yusuf’s post as “straightforward racism”.

Asked by the presenter, Jon Sopel, for his thoughts on the message, Reynolds said: “Pretty straightforward racism, isn’t it? There’s a potential candidate referenced there; spent decades in this country, huge contribution to her local community, so I think that speaks for itself.”
When Sopel asked whether it was “plain racism”, Reynolds replied: “Absolutely.”

Yusuf has drawn significant criticism for his inflammatory comments on X in recent months, including from top Reform UK figures. Nadine Dorries, the former Conservative minister who defected to Reform UK last year, described the post about Abdi-Wali as “nasty”.
“It was a nasty tweet. Zia Yusuf is a brilliant man, and he’s a genius actually, and he’s an incredible communicator. I wish he closed down his Twitter account,” she told Times Radio.

blocks.caption: Dorries and Yusuf during a panel discussion at Reform’s conference in Birmingham on Saturday. Photograph: Will Colebourne/PA

blocks.text: Laila Cunningham, Reform’s candidate for mayor of London and the daughter of immigrants from Egypt, told the Standard: “I don’t know what he meant by that comment. I read it a few times.
“I didn’t understand what he meant by that comment. Of course, you know, that woman is British. She’s the leader of Camden council. I didn’t understand what he meant by that.”
Reform UK has been contacted for comment.

Abdi-Wali arrived in Camden as a child refugee from Somalia. She has worked for more than a decade as a volunteer and trustee for local charities and is a governor of two schools in the borough, according to Labour.

She was first elected as a councillor in 2022 and became the leader of the council in May, when she said: “Camden has been my home for 35 years. It is the place that gave my family sanctuary, that welcomed us, and that has shaped so much of who I am, what I stand for and what inspired my commitment to public service and to working for the community that welcomed us.”

Labour is expected to announce its candidate for the Holborn and St Pancras byelection by Wednesday. It faces a battle against the Green party to retain the seat as Zack Polanski, its leader in England and Wales, is expected to be confirmed as its candidate.

The 11-year-old son of former PBA player Michael Mabulac continues to carve out a name for himself, turning heads with an impressive performance in the Korean Basketball League (KBL) Youth.

In July, Kael was one of only five Junior Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League (MPBL) players selected to represent Busan KCC Egis in the KBL Youth, alongside Josh Cruz, Kenan Picazo, Jaiden Dimalanta, and Cholo Evangelista across different age categories.
Kael showed why he deserved the spot, leading the under-11 division in points (12.8), rebounds (9.4), and blocks (1.6) while ranking second in steals (2.6).

Kael steered the under-11 team of KCC, one of the most storied KBL franchises with a record-tying seven championships, to an unbeaten 4-0 run in the preliminary stage before it fell narrowly to eventual champions Seoul SK Knights in the semifinals.
“I was surprised and I was really happy because it’s a once-in-a-lifetime experience to play internationally even though I’m still young,” Kael told Rappler in Filipino.

Although Kael grew up around basketball, his father Michael — a Jose Rizal University standout who won three PBA championships with San Miguel and now plays for Biñan Tatak Gel in the MPBL — did not expect him to pursue the sport at such a young age.
In fact, Kael only started playing basketball in 2024, when a club competing in the City Hoops Basketball League needed a 2015-born player to complete its roster.
Michael said he was initially hesitant to let his son play, particularly because Kael had yet to receive any formal training.

“I was worried that he might embarrass himself because he had no training,” said Michael. “He might do all sorts of things — did he even know the rules of basketball? I was even thinking that he might end up shooting at the opposing team’s basket.”
But Kael held his own, and before long, he began outperforming his more experienced teammates.
“At first, I just watched daddy, and then I saw that playing seemed exciting and fun. I liked it too and it became something I did every day,” said Kael.

Seeing potential in his son, Michael eventually decided to put Kael through formal training — a decision that paid off as the younger Mabulac drew interest from several schools, including La Salle Green Hills, Xavier, Angelicum, La Salle Zobel, Mapua, and NU.

It also helps that Kael has a professional basketball player as a father, with Michael providing valuable advice that allows him to shake off bad habits and develop a more disciplined approach to the game.

“After every practice, I correct him. I tell him, ‘This is what you’re doing right and this is what you’re doing wrong.’ I think that’s one of his advantages, that his learning does not end in practice,” said Mabulac.

It did not take long for Kael to stand out, regularly posting triple-doubles and double-doubles across various leagues. One of his most notable performances came in the under-11 final of the Batang PBA, where he scored 45 points to lead Magnolia to the title.
Kael also earned back-to-back Most Valuable Player honors in his age division in the Junior MPBL Pocket League.
But it is not only in sports where Kael thrives.
According to his mother, Mori, Kael is also a consistent honor student at Lourdes School Quezon City, having finished fifth grade with high honors.

“He also qualifies for an academic scholarship. He’s already a scholar as a varsity player, but he also qualifies as an academic scholar. That makes me even more proud because he’s able to do both,” said Mori.

For Michael and Mori, it is important to let Kael enjoy being a child rather than push him too hard, allowing him to have fun, explore his interests, and develop at his own pace while balancing basketball and academics.
“When he doesn’t want to play or practice, I let him. He’s still a kid,” said Michael.

Like his idol, Gilas Pilipinas and Goyang Sono Skygunners star Kevin Quiambao, Kael dreams of playing professional basketball in the KBL. He also wants to compete in the Olympics and FIBA competitions.

Standing at 5-foot-6 and already possessing an all-around game, Kael appears to be on the right track, with KCC showing interest in him after a bone age assessment indicated promising growth potential.
According to Michael, Kael underwent the assessment in Korea and is projected to reach a height of up to 6-foot-7.

“I’m always asked what I want to be when I grow up. I always say that I want to play basketball. They ask me if there’s anything else I want to do, but I tell them, that’s really the only thing I want,” said Kael.
Michael, who knows the basketball scene all too well after spending more than a decade as a pro, believes that Kael can go as far as his perseverance will take him.
“I’m here to simply to guide him. I tell him, ‘You’re already lucky — you have the height and you already have scholarship opportunities.’ Hard work is the only thing he needs to add,” said Michael.

As Kael continues to climb the ranks and attract more attention, Mori hopes he remains grounded, reminding him that his career and talent can be taken away in an instant if he gets too full of himself.
Kael vows not to let that happen.
“I’ll always listen to them and follow their advice so I can continue to improve in both academics and sports and achieve my dreams when I grow up,” Kael said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Detox teas? Expert warns against quick-fix weight-loss products
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A health expert urged Filipinos seeking to lose weight to be cautious about products marketed as quick fixes and instead pay greater attention to their sleep, stress, and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A health expert urged Filipinos seeking to lose weight to be cautious about products marketed as quick fixes and instead pay greater attention to their sleep, stress, and sustainable lifestyle changes.

Dr. Nemencio Nicodemus Jr., an endocrinologist and professor at the University of the Philippines (UP) College of Medicine and attending consultant at the Philippine General Hospital (PGH), also warned the public against purchasing counterfeit versions of popular prescription weight-loss drugs.
According to Nicodemus, weight loss associated with slimming and “detox” teas may largely reflect water loss and altered bowel movements rather than meaningful reductions in body fat.
“Rapid water-weight loss from teas or extreme diets is not equivalent to durable fat loss, and short-term results are unlikely to persist without lasting changes in behavior and lifestyle,” he said.
Nicodemus said diet teas were found to rely on mechanisms such as metabolic stimulation, appetite suppression, or laxative and diuretic effects rather than validated fat-loss pathways.

He cited a 2026 content analysis that found that 91.7 percent of sampled diet teas contained senna leaf, a laxative used to treat occasional constipation, despite being marketed with “natural” slimming imagery.
Laxatives promote bowel movements, while diuretics increase the amount of salt and water excreted through urine. Both can cause a temporary drop in weight without necessarily reducing body fat.
There were also reported cases of supposedly natural weight-loss products linked to adverse effects, including acute hepatitis in a teenager associated with Chinese green tea consumption.
The safety of prescription weight-loss drugs is another concern, according to Nicodemus, particularly amid the circulation of counterfeit and falsified medicines.
GLP-1 receptor agonist medications, such as semaglutide, and dual agonists, such as tirzepatide, have become increasingly associated with weight loss.
Both semaglutide and tirzepatide are prescribed for the treatment of type 2 diabetes but have been used off-label as weight-loss medications.

Based on data from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), there are only three registered brands of semaglutide: Ozempic, Wegovy, and Rybelsus, which are all manufactured by Danish pharmaceutical company Novo Nordisk.
Meanwhile, there is only one brand of tirzepatide registered with the FDA: Mounjaro, which is manufactured by Italy-based BSP Pharmaceuticals.
Nicodemus cited gastrointestinal effects as among the most common concerns, found in 20 percent to 40 percent of patients using higher-dose formulations of semaglutide.
A systematic review of 10 randomized controlled trials involving 14,550 participants, including 7,830 who received semaglutide, found that patients experienced nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting.
Semaglutide was also associated with an increased risk of gallbladder-related disorders, including gallstones.
The World Health Organization issued a medical product alert in June 2024 over falsified Ozempic products circulating globally, including in the Philippines.
Consumers who obtain semaglutide through informal online channels may face additional risks, including counterfeit products, incorrect active ingredients, contamination, and improper storage.
Nicodemus said weight management cannot be reduced to calorie counting.
Hormones, muscle mass, genetics, metabolism, sleep, stress, and lifestyle can interact to affect how a person gains, loses, and maintains weight, he said.
Nicodemus recommends a regular sleep cycle and stress management.
“Unregulated stress and lack of sleep increase cortisol levels. This makes the body less responsive to insulin, making it difficult to control blood sugar,” he said. /mcm

articles.title: NDRRMC: Southwest monsoon, cyclones leave 43 dead
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The death toll from the combined effects of the southwest monsoon and cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng, and Pilandok has reached 43, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The death toll from the combined effects of the southwest monsoon and cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng, and Pilandok has reached 43, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) reported on Sunday.

In its latest report, the NDRRMC said most of the deaths were recorded in Benguet due to landslides. Other fatalities were logged in La Union, Pangasinan, Zambales, Pampanga, Rizal, Batangas, Quezon, Oriental and Occidental Mindoro, Negros Occidental, and Caloocan.

The agency also said that 20 individuals were injured in Ilocos Sur, Benguet, Abra, Quezon City, Rizal, and Cavite due to landslides, fallen trees, strong currents, and vehicular accidents. Five individuals were also reported missing in Quezon City, Manila, Batangas, Rizal, and Pampanga.

The weather disturbances affected 10.2 million individuals, or 2.9 million families, in the National Capital Region, Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, Cordillera Administrative Region, Bicol Region, and Western Visayas.
The agency added that 62,300 individuals, or 18,100 families, are seeking temporary shelter in 807 evacuation centers.

The agency estimated the total cost of damage to infrastructure and agriculture at P7,790,000 and P4,130,000,000, respectively. It said a total of P2.59 billion worth of assistance was provided to affected families.
It also said that a state of calamity has been declared in 180 areas in Pangasinan, Benguet, Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga, Zambales, Tarlac, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro. /mcm

articles.title: Sara Duterte faces impeachment, criminal case, but ‘no double jeopardy’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte faces cases on similar grounds before two courts, but the principle of “double jeopardy” would still not apply. Impeachment spokesperson Reginald…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte faces cases on similar grounds before two courts, but the principle of “double jeopardy” would still not apply.
Impeachment spokesperson Reginald Tongol made this clear on Sunday as Duterte faced a grave threats case before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court and the Senate Impeachment Court.

Duterte’s alleged threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., his wife, Liza, and his cousin, former Rep. Martin Romualdez, made during an online press conference in November 2024, led to her legal battles on two different fronts.
“The principle of ‘double jeopardy’ does not apply,” Tongol told reporters. “Double jeopardy strictly applies to successive criminal proceedings.”

“We are distinct from regular courts; the Impeachment Court is a sui generis (unique) constitutional tribunal with the supreme mandate to determine political accountability and fitness for office, not penal liability,” he continued.
Tongol also noted that Article XI, Section 3, Paragraph 7 of the 1987 Constitution and a Supreme Court ruling provide that “criminal prosecution can proceed independently of impeachment.”
On Saturday, Duterte personally appeared to post P360,000 bail, or P120,000 each for three counts of grave threats, before Quezon City RTC Branch 98.
Her court appearance came as the court issued an arrest warrant against her on Friday.
These developments, Tongol said, “have absolutely zero legal implication on the ongoing impeachment trial.”
“They do not legally alter, pause, or dictate the Impeachment Court’s timeline,” he said.
If convicted before the Impeachment Court, Duterte will be removed from office and barred from holding any public post.
She is the first one to announce her presidential bid.

articles.title: Gatchalian to PNP: Take VP Duterte’s threats claim seriously
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Sunday called on the Philippine National Police to take Vice President Sara Duterte’s claims of threats seriously amid the issuance of an…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Sunday called on the Philippine National Police to take Vice President Sara Duterte’s claims of threats seriously amid the issuance of an arrest warrant against her over grave threats charges.
He stressed that everyone should feel safe in the country.

“The most important thing for me is the safety of everyone, including our vice president. That is the most important thing. If there is a threat to our vice president, a threat to her life, to her family, that should be taken seriously,” he said in an interview with dzBB on Sunday.

“I’m calling on the police to investigate on their own where the alleged threats were coming from because this is not good. Anybody, whether it is the vice president or an ordinary person, our government should protect them from any threats and anything bad that may happen to them. We want a society that is safe,” Gatchalian added.
Sought for comment on the timing of the issuance of the arrest warrant against Duterte, the Senate president said the investigations being conducted by other agencies cannot be controlled.

“There are simultaneous investigations happening, so we cannot control how these investigations go. Depending on the evidence they gather, how airtight these cases are, we cannot control that. In the impeachment court, we just keep going,” he said, adding that they aim to finish the trial before December. /mcm
