articles.title: Cotabato leaders call for unity in public service
articles.summary: DAVAO CITY – North Cotabato provincial leaders urged residents to uphold unity, faith, and dedication to public service during the 112th Founding Anniversary and the culmination of the Kalivungan…

blocks.text: DAVAO CITY – North Cotabato provincial leaders urged residents to uphold unity, faith, and dedication to public service during the 112th Founding Anniversary and the culmination of the Kalivungan Festival 2026 at the Provincial Capitol on Tuesday, Sept 1.

Cotabato Governor Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza, Vice Governor Rochella Marie Taliño-Taray, and Rep. Maria Alana Samantha Taliño-Santos highlighted the province's commitment to peace, progress, and unity during the program at The Basket.

blocks.caption: The Provincial Government of Cotabato, led by Governor Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza, vows to strengthen partnerships with government agencies and other stakeholders to advance peace, progress, and unity in the province as it culminates the 112th Founding Anniversary and Kalivungan Festival 2026 on Tues…

blocks.text: The Provincial Government of Cotabato, led by Governor Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza, vows to strengthen partnerships with government agencies and other stakeholders to advance peace, progress, and unity in the province as it culminates the 112th Founding Anniversary and Kalivungan Festival 2026 on Tuesday, September 1, at the Provincial Capitol Grounds in Amas, Kidapawan City. (Photo via Ivy Tejano / MB)

In a speech, Mendoza urged government workers and officials to perform their duties to the best of their ability, regardless of their positions, saying every contribution matters in advancing the province. "No matter how small or big your role is."

Mendoza emphasized that public service is a public trust. She said 112 years is such a long number and that they are blessed to have the presence and prayers of their priests and elders as they celebrate this milestone.

"Amid these crises, our faith in God can help us remain strong," she said, thanking local officials, national agencies, partnered organizations, and other stakeholders for their endless support to the province's development.

The governor welcomed the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Undersecretary, Fatima Aliah Dimaporo, who represented DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian as the guest of honor and speaker during the celebration.

Gatchalian, in a speech read by Dimaporo, congratulated the provincial government and its people on the province's 112th founding anniversary, highlighting everyone's role in building a legacy of peace, progress, and unity.

"Cotabato's 112-year history is shaped by the contributions of its farmers, workers, entrepreneurs, and communities, whose cooperation has helped build a stronger, more peaceful, and prosperous province," Gatchalian said.

Taray described the event as a celebration of Cotabato's diverse cultures, traditions, talents, and local products. She said their diverse languages, municipalities, and cultures should not divide their people, but bring them together as one community.

Santos said the anniversary should be measured not only by the scale of the festivities but also by the province's ability to bring its people together, remember its roots, and honor those who helped build its peace and progress.

Officials credited the collaborative efforts of the provincial government, district offices, local chief executives, national government partners, and other stakeholders in pursuing development and ensuring that families are not left behind.

The province's 112th Founding Anniversary and Kalivungan Festival 2026, dubbed "A Legacy of Peace, Progress, and Unity," underscores the province's ongoing efforts to build on its gains and strengthen solidarity among its communities.

Makilala emerges as champion of the Drum and Lyre Corps Competition and takes home the P300,000 cash prize during the culmination of the festival at the Provincial Capitol Grounds in Amas, Kidapawan City, on Tuesday morning.

They also won the special awards for Best in Street Parade, Best in Choreography, and Best in Musicality. Meanwhile, Mlang placed first runner-up and received P200,000, while Tulunan National High School finished second runner-up with P150,000.

articles.title: Six killed, several injured in Dumalinao road crash
articles.summary: ZAMBOANGA CITY- Six persons were killed while several others were injured when a passenger van crashed into a parked wing van truck in Dumalinao, Zamboanga del Sur on Tuesday, September 1. Witnesses…

blocks.text: (Photo via Liza Jocson)
ZAMBOANGA CITY- Six persons were killed while several others were injured when a passenger van crashed into a parked wing van truck in Dumalinao, Zamboanga del Sur on Tuesday, September 1.
Witnesses said the van was travelling from Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay when it collided with the other van that was parked along the road.
The impact was so severe that five persons were immediately killed. One expired while undergoing treatment at a medical facility.
Several persons were also treated at the hospital for injuries.
Investigation showed that a passenger van was travelling from Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay toward Pagadian City when the driver lost control of the vehicle.
The passenger van crashed into a wing van parked along the highway before colliding with other vehicles along the road.
Police are investigating other circumstances behind the road mishap.
Related Tags

articles.title: San Miguel, Aboitiz units win bids for Meralco’s 600-MW supply deal
articles.summary: Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) selected three power generators affiliated with San Miguel Corp. and Aboitiz Power Corp. to supply its 600-megawatt baseload requirement after they submitted the lowest…

blocks.text: Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) selected three power generators affiliated with San Miguel Corp. and Aboitiz Power Corp. to supply its 600-megawatt baseload requirement after they submitted the lowest offers in a competitive selection process.

In a statement, Meralco said Mariveles Power Gen Corp., Sual Power Inc., and GNPower Mariveles Energy Center emerged with the most competitive prices among six participants that submitted formal proposals.
Nine entities had originally expressed interest in the auction.

Mariveles Power Gen, a joint venture between San Miguel and Meralco PowerGen Corp., offered the lowest total levelized cost of electricity at ₱5.3573 per kilowatt-hour for a 200-megawatt slice. Sual Power, controlled by San Miguel’s energy arm, proposed ₱5.4357 per kilowatt-hour for another 200 megawatts.

GNPower Mariveles, a unit of the Aboitiz Group, initially bid for the entire 600-megawatt mandate at ₱5.5789 per kilowatt-hour before trimming its allocation to 200 megawatts to allow the top three bidders to split the requirement equally.

The offers came in below the reserve price set for the tender, according to Meralco’s Bids and Awards Committee for Power Supply Agreements. Only Energy Development Corp. failed to match the ceiling rate among the participants, which also included Masinloc Power Co. at ₱5.6290 per kilowatt-hour for 200 megawatts and Therma Luzon Inc. at ₱5.6988 per kilowatt-hour for 194 megawatts.

The procurement is structured to secure long-term power delivery to stabilize retail power tariffs for the country’s largest electricity distribution utility. Delivery of the first 300-megawatt tranche is scheduled to begin on Feb. 26, 2028, with the remaining 300 megawatts slated for Feb. 26, 2029.

The submissions underwent strict pass-fail completeness assessments and pre-qualification evaluations to ensure the procurement yields the least-cost electricity for consumers, said Lawrence S. Fernandez, chairman of Meralco’s power supply bidding committee. The panel conducted the bidding in line with guidelines set by the Department of Energy and the Energy Regulatory Commission.

The winning bids will undergo a post-qualification evaluation before the committee submits its final recommendation to Meralco’s board of directors for formal approval. Following board approval and the issuance of notices of award, the resulting 15-year power supply agreements will be submitted to regulators for final review and clearance before execution. (Gabriell Christel Galang)

articles.title: Boomers, Tall Blacks sharpen Gilas for Asian Qualifiers second round
articles.summary: Iron sharpens iron. And for Gilas Pilipinas, its experience in the first round of the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers against New Zealand and Australia certainly came in handy for the Nationals…

blocks.text: Iron sharpens iron.

And for Gilas Pilipinas, its experience in the first round of the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers against New Zealand and Australia certainly came in handy for the Nationals in their 2-0 sweep of the fourth window.

The Filipinos may have come out with a 2-4 record at the end of the first round of the qualifiers but Gilas believes playing to such a high level of competition allowed them to be ready for what was in store for them against Jordan and Iran in the second round.
“It was a lot of learning experience out there. I mean, those are the top two teams in the pool,” said Gilas star Dwight Ramos.
“We had tough opponents Australia and New Zealand but they made us better. We were able to come back from slow starts and we’re just very happy for the guys,” he added.

Before the August window, Gilas came in on a four-game losing skid in the qualifiers — all of those came at the hands of the two Oceania teams. The only victories Gilas had in the first round was against Guam.
The Boomers gave Gilas a beating in their two meetings, winning 93-66 on the road and then 96-42 at their home turf.
Against the Tall Blacks, it was more competitive with the Kiwis escaping 96-93 in the first meeting and then avoiding a homecourt upset with a 106-104 double-overtime win against Gilas.

As tough as the matches were, Ramos said the losses built Gilas character which finally paid off when they recovered from double-digit deficits in the 82-81 win over Jordan and the grindout 68-56 victory over Iran.

“We all believe in each other so whoever's out there on the court, looks like they're playing with confidence. Make or miss, it doesn't matter 'cause you know as teammates we're here behind them and we're always making up and picking each other up,” explained Ramos.
“It feels good 'cause it's been a while since we did that. It feels good. You know, (we) start winning games again. We gotta tough windows and feels like we're getting our groove,” he added.

articles.title: Stocks snap 4-day loss as factory output hits decade high
articles.summary: Local stocks snapped a four-day losing streak, surging more than two percent as investors rushed to snap up beaten-down shares following data showing factory activity expanded at its fastest pace in…

blocks.text: Local stocks snapped a four-day losing streak, surging more than two percent as investors rushed to snap up beaten-down shares following data showing factory activity expanded at its fastest pace in nearly a decade.
The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) gained 137.56 points, or 2.31 percent, to close at 6,093.89 on Tuesday, Sept. 1.
Mining and banking equities led the advance, providing enough muscle to lift the headline gauge even as half of the market’s sub-sectors closed in negative territory.

Trading activity picked up sharply, with turnover reaching 1.88 billion shares valued at ₱10.47 billion. Market breadth was positive, as advancers outpaced decliners 106 to 88, while 64 issues ended unchanged.

The sharp turnaround came as market participants moved to capitalize on discounted valuations among premier issues following last week's relentless selling pressure, according to Luis Limlingan, managing director at Regina Capital Development Corp.

Investor sentiment got a significant boost from macro data released earlier in the day. The S&P Global Philippines Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index jumped to 54.9 in August from 51.8 in July, marking a fourth straight month of operational expansion. A reading above 50 signals growth.

The August figure was the strongest reading for the factory sector since December 2016. The index serves as a reliable leading economic indicator, signaling an accelerating pickup in broader commercial output.

Analysts noted that the strong reading aligns with recent record-high export volumes, driven in large part by the global boom in artificial intelligence infrastructure, high-end electronics, and semiconductor shipments.
The manufacturing expansion helped relieve growing anxieties surrounding local macroeconomic growth momentum, added Japhet Tantiangco, research manager at Philstocks Financial Inc.

Lower valuations coupled with improving fundamentals created an attractive entry point for institutional and retail bargain hunters alike, allowing the benchmark index to reverse its recent downward trajectory.

articles.title: Questions abound for Djokovic after US Open loss, 3 years without Grand Slam title
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic waved goodbye, made a heart shape with his hands and blew kisses to the crowd as he walked off the court inside Arthur Ashe Stadium to a standing ovation. Among those applauding in…

blocks.text: Novak Djokovic waved goodbye, made a heart shape with his hands and blew kisses to the crowd as he walked off the court inside Arthur Ashe Stadium to a standing ovation.

Among those applauding in return were Djokovic’s 11-year-old son Stefan, while his 8-year-old daughter Tara covered her eyes and loaded her floppy-eared stuffed animal into a bag that went around her shoulder.
Back down on the court, Djokovic had his two black bags — one containing his rackets and the other more equipment — hanging from his shoulders.

After his first-round loss to Mariano Navone at the U.S. Open on Sunday night, it remains to be seen whether the 39-year-old Djokovic will ever bring those bags out on a court again for a professional match.

The 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 loss marked Djokovic’s earliest Grand Slam exit in two decades — dating back to the 2006 Australian Open — and the first time ever that he lost his opener at the U.S. Open.
The holder of a men's record 24 Grand Slam singles titles, Djokovic has now gone three straight years without winning a major.
Physical issues

Perhaps even more concerning than his record — which has otherwise still been fairly competitive since his last Grand Slam title at the 2023 U.S. Open — is that Djokovic has consistently struggled with physical issues this year.

After a run to the Australian Open final to start the year, Djokovic played little because of an injured right shoulder. Then he appeared weakened by a Paris heat wave in a five-set loss to Brazilian teenager Joao Fonseca in the third round of the French Open.
“I was barely standing on my legs toward the end of the match,” Djokovic said after getting beaten by Fonseca.

Djokovic revived himself for a run to the semifinals at Wimbledon and then struggled again at the Cincinnati Open this month when he was beaten by 50th-ranked Thiago Agustin Tirante in his opening match.
After the loss to Tirante, Djokovic said an unspecified health condition made it difficult for him to play in hot and humid weather.

“It’s just a condition that I have, health-wise, that has been bothering me for the past couple of years,” Djokovic said. “A lot of issues, especially when it is humid and it is hot. … Nerves and everything involved that make it worse.”

Djokovic’s issues against Navone began midway through the first set when he appeared to be struggling with the heat and humidity. Djokovic led early on in the first set but Navone got back on serve before the match was briefly halted for the roof to be closed because of light rain.
As Djokovic sat in his chair during the break, he kept moving an ice pack around his face, head and neck.

Navone won the first in a tiebreaker and things eventually got much worse for Djokovic, who threw up at least once and later appeared to be cramping when he grabbed at his left foot. Djokovic swallowed pills brought to him by a doctor and had his lower back massaged during a medical timeout between the fourth and fifth sets, and he grimaced after several shots.
Djokovic made 70 unforced errors in a painful performance that ended a few minutes before midnight.

“It’s something that I’ve been carrying, unfortunately, pretty much every match this year: vomiting, throwing up, a serious issue there,” Djokovic said. “Then my whole body starts to collapse, basically cramping and pain. Yeah, the back just gave up in the end and shoulder, and I couldn’t close it out.”
What's next?

Where does Djokovic go from here? While he hasn’t openly discussed an imminent retirement, one final hurrah at the Australian Open — the Grand Slam tournament he’s won a record 10 times — in January would be a fitting setting for a final send-off.
Or he could continue competing into his 40s.
After all, Djokovic has reached two Grand Slam finals and six semifinals over the last three years.
“I feel when I’m healthy, I’m still able to play as a top-five player, still able to compete at the highest level,” Djokovic said after his semifinal loss to Jannik Sinner at Wimbledon this year.
Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal's physical issues
Djokovic is the last man still competing among the Big Three players who dominated the game over the last two decades.
Roger Federer (knee) and Rafael Nadal (hip) also struggled with physical issues before they retired in 2022 and 2024, respectively. Federer was 41 when he stopped and Nadal was 38.
Djokovic’s 24 major titles are two more than Nadal’s 22 and four more than Federer’s 20. Those numbers prompt some to consider Djokovic tennis' GOAT.

“That’s OK. He has done incredible,” Federer said last week. “It’s amazing what he has been able to do and still now. I would have thought that maybe he was getting to a place where all of a sudden we would see a much bigger decline.”
Now — perhaps — Djokovic is declining more severely.

articles.title: Romualdez lawyer counters Clavano, says recantations don't boost Ombudsman's case
articles.summary: The counsel of Leyte 1st district Rep. Martin Romualdez has assailed the notion that the recantations of Orly Guteza and several members of the so-called “Maleta Boys” strengthen the complaint…

blocks.text: The counsel of Leyte 1st district Rep. Martin Romualdez has assailed the notion that the recantations of Orly Guteza and several members of the so-called “Maleta Boys” strengthen the complaint against the former House Speaker in connection with the flood control projects corruption scandal.
"Well, we respectfully disagree po," lawyer Ade Fajardo, a former national president of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP), said in a statement Tuesday, Sept. 1.

Fajardo was referring to Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano’s position that the original statements and the recantations should both be treated as evidence in the Office of the Ombudsman’s preliminary investigation into Romualdez’s alleged anomalous flood control projects payoffs.
Clavano has said that a recantation is “not an eraser” but "additional evidence" because the original statement and the later version must be placed side by side to determine which is true.
But Fajardo said that comparison should expose, not cure, the conflicts in the witness' accounts.
A witness who first claimed personal knowledge and later denied the central allegation creates a credibility issue that investigators must resolve before filing a case, he said.

Fajardo rejected the position that the witnesses’ withdrawal of their earlier allegations could somehow bolster the evidence against Romualdez. He noted that the recantations instead raised questions about the very statements previously used to implicate the former Speaker.
“Mukhang nagsasabi lang ang tanggapan ng Ombudsman ng mga ganoong salita para sabihin na buhay pa ang kaso nito,” the Romualdez lawyer said.
(It seems that the Office of the Ombudsman is only saying such things to make it appear that the case is still alive.)
According to the ex-IBP offcial, a witness who withdraws or disowns an earlier account does not automatically provide stronger evidence against the person previously accused.

Rather, the recantations should be examined for what they say about the credibility and reliability of the original allegations, particularly when the witnesses themselves are now disputing or withdrawing their previous statements.
It's all about evidence

Fajardo maintained that the strength of a case must rest on competent evidence that independently links Romualdez to the alleged wrongdoing, and not on the mere characterization of recantations as new or additional evidence.
The two-time former Speaker has repeatedly denied the accusations against him and maintained that the complaints should be resolved on the basis of evidence and due process.
Fajardo said the fundamental question remains whether there is credible and sufficient evidence directly linking Romualdez to the alleged offenses.

Guteza, who testified in September 2025 Senate Blue Ribbon Committee hearing, withdrew his allegation that he had participated in the delivery of cash-filled suitcases (maleta) to an alleged residence associated with Romualdez. Several former security aides of ex-Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co have also recanted earlier accounts involving alleged cash deliveries.

Romualdez’s Aug. 20 supplemental counter-affidavit placed those reversals beside 25 sworn statements from other former Co drivers and security aides. The 25 denied any knowledge of or participation in the delivery of money to Romualdez or any politician or government official.
Some were people identified in earlier statements as companions in alleged delivery trips, but they denied taking part.
“Sa aming estimation, sa aming appreciation ng mga recantation na 'yan, ang aming position ay talagang wala pong kaso na, sobrang hina na,” Fajardo said.
(Based on our assessment, our appreciation of those recantations, our position is that there really is no case anymore, it has become extremely weak.)

articles.title: With elections nearing, battleground Republicans still waiting for Trump to open his campaign wallet
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — When Vice President JD Vance stepped on stage in Michigan on Monday, it was MAGA Inc. writing the check for the campaign event. It was a rare bit of spending in a battleground state…

blocks.text: LAS VEGAS (AP) — When Vice President JD Vance stepped on stage in Michigan on Monday, it was MAGA Inc. writing the check for the campaign event. It was a rare bit of spending in a battleground state from a powerful political organization that has mostly been missing in action this year.
With just over two months to go before the midterm elections, President Donald Trump is still sitting on most of his colossal war chest, and he's been growing his money pile instead of spending it.

Even though the president and his team insist they'll open their wallet soon, frustrations are growing as Republicans try to maintain control of Congress despite headwinds partially of Trump's own creation. While the president remains the party's best asset in turning out its base, he is historically unpopular, with low marks on his handling of the economy and the ongoing war in Iran that most Americans say was not worth fighting.
The ticking clock narrows Republicans' options because time on the airwaves gets more limited and more expensive as the election draws near.
"Hope springs eternal," said Republican donor Dan Eberhart, one of many who have been left wondering about the president's plans.

Texas is a particular issue, especially after Trump helped scandal-plagued state Attorney General Ken Paxton beat incumbent Sen. John Cornyn, turning what was supposed to be a safe Republican seat into a potential toss up.

Democratic nominee James Talarico has dramatically outraised Paxton, bringing in more than $68.5 million to Paxton's $9 million. Talarico had more than $21.5 million cash on hand at the end of June, versus Paxton's $1.75 million.

"We need help from the president," Sen. John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, told Fox News over the weekend. "I'm hoping that the president is going to spend $100 or $200 million in Texas, but he hasn't committed to it yet."
MAGA Inc. is the country's biggest political war chest

MAGA Inc. had more than $403 million at the end of July, according to the latest campaign finance filings, having brought in another $3 million over the course of the month and having spent practically nothing. That's more cash than any of the major party committees.

Its only major outlay so far has been in South Carolina, where the group invested nearly $830,000 on a last-minute get-out-the-vote push to help Sen. Darline Graham win the Republican nomination to succeed her late brother Lindsey Graham. The sum included about $774,000 on get-out-the-vote phone calls and $53,500 on text messages.
In the meantime, Trump has continued to raise money.
He headlined a Republican National Committee fundraiser in Texas last Thursday and participated in several MAGA Inc. meetings and a dinner at his golf course in Virginia on Saturday.
The group announced last week that it is planning to hold a series of rallies in battleground states, which started Monday with the Michigan event headlined by Vance.
MAGA Inc. will be spending in competitive races, according to an operative familiar with the group's plans who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the yet-to-be-announced investments.
That is expected to include ads highlighting the president and his accomplishments, which he has pushed to focus on despite his low approval ratings, a strategy first reported by The Atlantic.
The delay could have consequences

Some Republican campaign vendors such as advertisers, direct mail companies and canvassing firms were told in August by MAGA Inc. leaders to be ready for action. But they have not been made aware of a comprehensive plan, according to people with knowledge of the situation who requested anonymity to discuss private deliberations.
The delays come with consequences. Advertising rates are much higher at this late date in the campaign than they were in the spring when other organizations reserved airtime.

Indeed, some Republican strategists familiar with the status of the president's still-developing plans said it is almost certainly too late for outside groups to even purchase advertising in key markets in Texas, where MAGA Inc. was asked by Senate Republican leadership to commit resources.

MAGA Inc. has been testing ads for Paxton, including one criticizing Talarico over rural hospital policy, but the ad has yet to air. People familiar with conversations said it might run online or on digital channels instead of on television.
While super PACs have traditionally spent big on television buys, the group also has other options.

Because the runoff campaign was so brief, the MAGA Inc. team worked to appeal directly to voters who feel loyal to Trump but are less likely to vote in non-presidential elections. Aides have discussed a similar approach in Texas, focused on outreach such as neighborhood canvassing, phone calls and mail specifically targeting those low-propensity voters, according to people with knowledge of the discussions.
Some Republican operatives who otherwise worry about limited time believe such an effort could make a difference as long as MAGA Inc. commits a significant amount of money to the effort.
Trump promises to spend money
The president and his team have said the money is coming soon.
"Of course," Trump said when recently asked by Punchbowl News. "I'm going to help Republicans."
James Blair, the former White House deputy chief of staff who left to run Trump's midterm operation, has also said money is on its way.

"The president is going to expend substantial resources to win the midterms," he said in June on "The Sean Spicer Show." "He cares deeply about the party winning, and anything he can do to support that he's going to do and is already doing."
But Trump also has incentives to keep much of the money he has amassed.

As a lame-duck president constitutionally barred from running for a third term, maintaining a commanding sum in the bank would help him to continue to wield power. He proved this cycle that he is extremely adept at ousting members he opposes, and Republican candidates could continue traveling to Mar-a-Lago to seek his blessing in the years ahead.
As Trump told Punchbowl News about his campaign cash, "I can spend it on pretty much anything I want."

articles.title: P14.28M drug haul intercepted in Manila
articles.summary: A 33-year-old drug suspect was arrested, and more than two kilograms of shabu worth P14.28 million were seized in a buy-bust operation in Ermita, Manila, on Monday, Aug. 31, the Manila Police…

blocks.text: A 33-year-old drug suspect was arrested, and more than two kilograms of shabu worth P14.28 million were seized in a buy-bust operation in Ermita, Manila, on Monday, Aug. 31, the Manila Police District (MPD) said.
The MPD identified the suspect as “George,” alias “Kapatid,” a resident of Navotas City.

According to MPD Chief Brig. Gen. Arnold Santiago, the suspect initially conducted a transaction in the southern part of Metro Manila before moving to the Manila area, where MPD Drug Enforcement Unit operatives tracked and arrested him.
Santiago said the operation resulted in the recovery of two kilograms of suspected shabu valued at P14.28 million.

Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno” Domagoso praised Santiago and the MPD Drug Enforcement Unit operatives for successfully conducting the operation while keeping both the suspect and police personnel safe.
Domagoso said the seizure prevented a large volume of illegal drugs from potentially reaching communities in Manila.
“Wag kami, wag sa Maynila (Don’t mess with us. Not in the city of Manila),” Domagoso said during his “Talk to the People” program at Manila City Hall.
“We are always certain about our policy, we are certain about our rules and we will continue to fulfill our obligation with regard to the peace and order situation of our city,” he added.
Domagoso also warned individuals involved in illegal activities against operating in Manila.

“Kung gusto niyo naman, magbagong buhay na kayo. Call naman kami kung gusto niyo kami subukin sa Maynila (If you want to start a new life, then do so. But if you want to test us in Manila, go ahead),” he said.
He said the city government would continue working with the MPD to prevent illegal drugs from becoming available in the city.

“Sa mga nanay at tatay na nanonood, isa po itong tagumpay ng ating Manila Police District at siyudad ng Maynila na hindi maging available itong mga ipinagbabawal na droga sa lungsod ng Maynila (To the mothers and fathers watching, this is a victory for the Manila Police District and the city of Manila in keeping illegal drugs out of the city),” Domagoso said.

He congratulated Santiago and the MPD Drug Enforcement Unit operatives involved in the drug bust, saying the operation was another step toward keeping large quantities of illegal drugs away from Manila residents.
Domagoso also credited the MPD for continuing its peace and order efforts despite the flooding, bad weather and other challenges faced by the city over the weekend.

“Habang may delubyo, may aberya, tayo’y kinakaharap ang hamon sa kalsada dala ng pagbaha, mga sakit at infection, ang inyong Manila Police District ay hindi po tumitigil upang maipatupad ang kapanatagan ng pamumuhay sa Manila (While there are disasters and difficulties, as we face challenges on the streets brought by flooding, illnesses and infections, your Manila Police District does not stop working to ensure peaceful living in Manila),” he said.
Earlier, Domagoso reminded Manila residents to take precautions amid the prevailing conditions, urging them to wear masks as much as possible and stay indoors whenever possible.
Meanwhile, Domagoso announced the arrest of another wanted person by the MPD at Barangay Malanday in Marikina City.
The suspect was identified as 54-year-old Carlos Castillo, a resident of Tondo, Manila, who had been the subject of a warrant of arrest issued on Jan. 14, 2026.
The arrest was carried out by personnel of MPD Police Station 14 with the assistance of barangay officials in Marikina City.
Domagoso said the case involved a 14-year-old female victim.
He thanked the barangay officials who assisted the police in locating and apprehending Castillo, who had allegedly been hiding for more than a year.
The mayor said Castillo would be brought before the court and that authorities would inform the issuing court about his apprehension.
He also warned individuals who have outstanding warrants against them to surrender rather than continue hiding from authorities.

“Kung kayo’y may mga nagawang krimen o tinakbuhan ng husgado at na-issue ang warrant of arrest, basta payo ko sa inyo sumuko na kayo (If you have committed crimes or evaded the court and a warrant of arrest has been issued against you, my advice is to surrender),” Domagoso said.
He warned that individuals who commit crimes outside Manila and attempt to hide in the city would also not be spared.
“Kung ginawa niyo sa ibang bayan at dito kayo magtatago ay hindi rin kayo welcome (If you committed a crime in another town and come here to hide, you are not welcome here either),” he said.
Domagoso congratulated Santiago, Col. Pura, and the MPD personnel involved in the arrest.

“If you’re a criminal in Manila, kahit saan sulok, lupalok, patkueba pa kayo magpunta, it’s just a matter of time mauhuhuli-mauhuhuli kayo ng Manila Police District (wherever you go, no matter what corner or remote place you hide in, it is just a matter of time before the Manila Police District catches you),” Domagoso said.
The mayor also announced that the MPD received recognition at the regional level for its implementation of local laws and ordinances.
According to Domagoso, the MPD ranked first in the implementation of local ordinances.
He said the recognition reflected the police district’s efforts to enforce local laws in Manila and congratulated Santiago and his personnel for the accomplishment.
“Number one po ang Manila Police District sa implementation ng local ordinances (The Manila Police District is number one in the implementation of local ordinances)," Domagoso said.
He urged the MPD to continue its enforcement efforts and maintain peace and order in the city.
Domagoso said the police district’s work remained important even as Manila dealt with flooding, health concerns and other challenges brought by the recent weather conditions.

“In our own little way, habang may delubyo, may aberya, tayo’y kinakaharap ang hamon sa kalsada dala ng pagbaha, mga sakit at infection, ang inyong Manila Police District ay hindi po tumitigil upang maipatupad ang kapanatagan ng pamumuhay sa Manila (In our own little way, while there are disasters and difficulties, as we face challenges on the streets brought by flooding, illnesses and infections, your Manila Police District does not stop working to ensure peaceful living in Manila),” he said.
He also thanked the families of police personnel for supporting their loved ones who serve in the MPD.

“Sa mga pamilya ng police, I thank you very much sa inyo for supporting your father, your mother or your son for doing a very good job being a member of the Manila Police District (To the families of police officers, I thank you very much for supporting your father, mother or son for doing a very good job as a member of the Manila Police District),” Domagoso said.
He urged Manila residents to remain cautious and safe as the city continues to face the effects of the recent weather disturbances.

“Mag-iingat po kayo at pagpalainawa kayo ng buong may kapal. Maraming salamat po. Manila, God first! (Please stay safe and may God bless you all. Thank you very much. Manila, God first!).” Domagoso said. (Shane Quiachon)

articles.title: Public service is not measured by what leaders wear during disaster response—Palace
articles.summary: What leaders wear during disaster response should not be the basis for judging their public service, a Palace official said. In a press briefing on Tuesday, Sept. 1, Palace Press Officer and…

blocks.text: What leaders wear during disaster response should not be the basis for judging their public service, a Palace official said.

In a press briefing on Tuesday, Sept. 1, Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro was asked about Malacañang's position on government officials who were seen wearing designer clothes while inspecting flood-hit areas.
Castro was quick to say that President Marcos "has no message about that."
This, as she argued, is not measured by the clothes politicians wear during post-calamity rounds.

"Ang pagse-serbisyo po ay hindi po nakikita sa damit. Nakikita po ito sa gawa, nakikita po ito kung visible ba iyong mga leaders at nandidiyan sila para tumulong (Public service is not measured by the clothes a leader wears. It is seen in their actions and it is seen whether leaders are visible and present to help)," Castro said.

"Maybe, ang sasabihin ng iba: bakit designer clothes pa ang suot. But sabi nga natin, hindi po nakikita ang pagtulong, ang serbisyong totoo sa damit ng isang lider (Some may say: why are they wearing designer clothes. But as we have said, genuine help and true public service are not reflected in a leader’s clothing)," Castro added.
The Palace official also argued that some people may look very simple, wearing just a T-shirt and pants, or even getting soaked in the rain, "but they may not actually be helping anyone."
"So mas maganda po na tingnan ang lider sa trabaho, sa gawa, hindi po sa damit (So it is better to judge a leader by their work and actions, not by their outfit)," Castro further said.
'They also need to be sensitive'
Castro said she cannot speak for officials who wear branded clothing, adding that they know what they should do and how they should interact with their constituents.
However, she said, officials must "also need to be sensitive" in times of calamities, grief, or trauma.

"Hindi natin alam kung ang pagsusuot ng branded na iyan ay mura na sa kanila. So, depende, depende sa kanila, baka iyan ay—kung sa atin na ordinaryong tao ay napakamahal, baka sa kanila ay mura lang iyan. dahil, iyan ang kanilang nakagawian (We do not know whether wearing branded clothing is actually inexpensive for them. It depends on their circumstances. What may be very expensive for ordinary people like us may be relatively cheap for them because it is simply what they are accustomed to wearing)," Castro said.

"But still, siguro kailangan din maging sensitive kasi lalong-lalo na, kung iyong mga kababayan natin ay nakakaramdam ng hirap, trauma at kalungkutan (Still, I think they also need to be sensitive, especially when our fellow citizens are experiencing hardship, trauma, and grief)," Castro added.
Pampanga Governor Lilia Pineda and son, Vice Governor Dennis Pineda, Drew flak for wearing designer clothes during inspections in flood-stricken areas in the province.
'Nothing wrong with coming together to pray' amid severe flooding

Malacañang said it respects Pineda's message to her constituents amid the massive flooding in the province, adding that there is nothing wrong with enjoining people to pray during severe weather conditions.
Castro said the Palace respects Pineda's remarks "because she is the one experiencing this firsthand."

In a TV interview, Pineda urged residents affected by flooding to pray, heed provincial government warnings, prepare, and protect their families, adding that they should not rely entirely on the government during calamities.

"Wala naman po sigurong masama kung talagang sama-sama rin tayong mananalangin dahil sabi nga po natin isa sa mga dahilan ng ganitong klaseng unos ay climate change – isa lamang ito maraming factors (There is certainly nothing wrong with all of us coming together in prayer, especially since, as we have said, one of the reasons for this kind of severe weather is climate change, although it is only one of many factors)," Castro said.

"At kailangan din po talaga lahat tayo ay nagtutulung-tulungan. Hindi po magagampanan ng gobyerno ang mailigtas kayong lahat kung ang iba nating mga kababayan ay sumusuway sa batas (And we really need everyone to work together. The government cannot save everyone if some of our fellow citizens continue to violate the law)," she added.
The Palace spokesperson reiterated the need to strictly follow the "No Build Zone" policy.

"So, kapag sinabi po natin na “No Build Zone” at iyan po ay delikado na kayo ay magpatayo ng bahay iyon po ay ibig sabihin na huwag na po kayong sumuway dahil kaligtasan ninyo rin po naman ang magiging issue dito (So, when we say 'No Build Zone,' and we say that it is dangerous to build a house in such an area, that means you should not disobey the rules because your own safety is ultimately at stake)," Castro said.

"So, ang nais ng Pangulo lahat po tayo ay tumupad sa batas, kapag tumupad naman tayo sa batas mas madali magagawaan ng paraan kung anuman ang magiging issue dahil sabay-sabay tayong nagtutulung-tulungan (The President’s message is for all of us to comply with the law. If we follow the law, it will be much easier to find solutions to whatever issues may arise because we will all be working together)," Castro added.
Castro further said that it would be difficult for the President to speak for others or dictate what local officials must say.

"Mahirap po kasing pangunahan ang Pangulo at magdikta ang Pangulo sa sasabihin ng bawat isa – sasabihin na naman nila nakikialam ang Pangulo sa kanilang freedom of expression (It would be difficult for the President to speak for others or dictate what each person should say. They would probably say again that the President is interfering with their freedom of expression)," Castro pointed out.

"So, nasa tao po iyan kung papaano niya po ibibigay ang kanyang mensahe sa mga kababayan natin na nakakaranas ng of course kalungkutan, kasawian, disappointment at ang Pangulo po naman ay ramdam po ang hinaing ng ating mga kababayan (So, it is up to each individual how they choose to deliver their message to our fellow citizens who are, of course, experiencing sadness, misfortune, and disappointment. The President, for his part, understands and feels the concerns of our fellow citizens)," Castro added.

articles.title: Rescuers comb through mud and debris as Nepal-China floods leave more than 1,000 dead
articles.summary: KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescue teams with search dogs combed through mud, rocks and debris Tuesday in Nepal and China looking for thousands of people still missing after catastrophic flooding tore…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescue teams with search dogs combed through mud, rocks and debris Tuesday in Nepal and China looking for thousands of people still missing after catastrophic flooding tore through communities across the Himalayas, leaving more than 1,000 dead.

Nepal's disaster agency said Tuesday that 987 deaths had been counted there, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreigners. Chinese authorities, in their latest update on Sunday, reported 16 deaths and 546 people still missing, including 261 foreigners.

The scale of last week's disaster was hampering rescue efforts in both regions, with landslides, destroyed roads and widespread damage cutting off remote areas. Crews faced challenging conditions as they searched unstable terrain and piles of debris, raising fears the death toll could rise as rescuers reach isolated communities.
Rescuers race to reach missing hydropower workers

In Nepal, rescuers were racing to reach hundreds of workers believed to be trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects damaged by the floods. About 900 workers are missing from 12 projects, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to Nepalese authorities.

Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal's army spokesperson, said teams assisted by foreign experts were working at several hydropower projects. Visuals released by the army showed rescue teams entering dark, debris-filled tunnels, wading through mud and water and climbing over rocks as they searched for signs of life.
On the Chinese side, rescue crews scoured areas hit by mudslides, particularly around the Gyirong Port border crossing, which was destroyed.

Some rescuers, aided by search dogs, searched gaps among rocks and debris for signs of life. Other teams used heavy machinery to clear a major highway leading to Gyirong Port, hoping to clear the way for equipment, personnel and supplies to reach the disaster zone, according to China's state-run Global Times newspaper.
Relief operations expand to reach stranded communities

At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far, according to Nepalese authorities. Emergency crews were using helicopters and other aircraft to reach stranded communities in areas where roads and bridges have been destroyed by the flooding and landslides.
Authorities on Tuesday also stepped up efforts to provide assistance to survivors in areas where roads and other transportation routes had been damaged or cut off.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said China's second batch of relief supplies for Nepal was expected to ship Tuesday, including drones, DNA testing and water purification equipment. Chinese DNA testing experts will also help Nepal identity bodies, he said.

Bimal Sharma, a helicopter pilot who has been flying rescue and relief missions since the disaster began, said he was shocked to see the devastation in Timure, a border town close to Tibet that he has known for years.
"It felt like I was flying over an entirely different landscape," he said.
Sharma said he has had little opportunity to speak with the people he rescued, but their expressions told him how deeply the disaster had affected them.
"I can see the pain in their eyes. It's heartbreaking," he said.
The disaster began with a glacial collapse high in the Himalayas
The Aug. 26 disaster began with a chain of events high in the Himalayas. A glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

Scientists studying satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have involved the failure of bedrock beneath a glacier in the Himalayan region. The rockfall was powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

The resulting surge of water and debris entered rivers that flow through valleys in Tibet and Nepal, causing them to rise rapidly. Floodwaters swept away homes, buildings, roads and bridges and carried mud and rocks downstream.

articles.title: DigiPlus unit prepares for new online gaming cash flow in partnership with IEC
articles.summary: DigiPlus Interactive Corp. is anticipating a second online gaming revenue stream this month when its wholly-owned subsidiary, Total Gamezone Xtreme Incorporated (TGXI), goes live with the online…

blocks.text: DigiPlus Interactive Corp. is anticipating a second online gaming revenue stream this month when its wholly-owned subsidiary, Total Gamezone Xtreme Incorporated (TGXI), goes live with the online gaming platform of International Entertainment Corporation’s (IEC) LaVie Resort & Casino Manila (formerly New Coast Hotel Manila).
IEC subsidiary New Coast Leisure Inc. (NCLI) holds the online gaming license, while TGXI will serve as the operator and gaming system administrator.

In a regulatory filing, IEC disclosed that NCLI and TGXI agreed on a gross gaming revenue (GGR) sharing ratio of three percent for NCLI and 97 percent for TGXI. This split is subject to applicable deductions, including the PAGCOR share, gaming license fees, audit fees, foundation fees, franchise taxes, and other related charges.

Under the Online Gaming License issued by the Electronic Gaming Licensing Department (EGLD) of the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR), NCLI is accredited to offer Electronic Casino Games, Electronic Bingo Games, Online Poker Games, and Specialty Games.

During the initial phase of operations, NCLI and TGXI will focus on Electronic Casino Games, anchored by Electronic Games—games of chance where outcomes are generated by a certified Random Number Generator (RNG). The roster also includes Table Games (traditional casino games played without live human dealers and delivered in an electronic visual format) and Arcade Games (specialty, non-traditional electronic games featuring simple mechanics and skill- or entertainment-based gameplay). All game categories run on computer-based software approved by PAGCOR.

IEC noted that these game offerings are currently in trial runs, with NCLI and TGXI actively refining operating procedures to resolve internal control deficiencies highlighted in a recent audit report.

While NCLI owns the Online Gaming Platform (OGP), TGXI provides the computer-based software and gaming content powering the platform. TGXI owns and controls the underlying assets used to supply, aggregate, integrate, and operate the offerings. At this stage, the NCLI-TGXI partnership does not cover land-based casino games streamed online by Integrated Resorts. However, the Group plans to expand into land-based electronic gaming terminals—including Online Table Games and Online Slot Machines—in its next phase. NCLI already holds provisional licenses for these IR gaming operations.
Brokerage firm Abacus Securities Corporation observed that "industry-wide gross gaming revenues have steadied in the last two quarters despite high inflation."

However, Abacus cautioned that "significant damage to property and livelihoods due to monsoon rains in the last few weeks will likely slow discretionary spending for the third quarter," while adding, "We also see Bloomberry's entry into online gaming as a significant risk."

articles.title: Senate finalizing new timetable for VP Sara impeachment trial
articles.summary: The Senate Impeachment Court is finalizing possible changes to the schedule of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial to fit the proceedings around the Senate’s legislative calendar.…

blocks.text: The Senate Impeachment Court is finalizing possible changes to the schedule of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial to fit the proceedings around the Senate’s legislative calendar.
(Senate PRIB photo)

Impeachment Court spokesperson Regie Tongol said the court has obtained the Senate Committee on Finance calendar to help Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian and Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero determine how to schedule the trial going forward.
“The impeachment court is actually finalizing kung ano po yung actual na changes if ever may mangyayari po (what the actual changes are if such things will happen),” Tongol said.
Tongol said several options are being considered, including moving the trial entirely to the afternoon, retaining the current schedule while adding hearing days, or adopting a mixed schedule.
Under the mixed arrangement, some trial sessions could be held in the morning while others would take place in the afternoon.

“So puwede pong mangyari malipat po sa hapon, totally yung hearing, mag-stay po [sa day], o kaya naman po mix po. May mga araw po na umaga, may mga araw naman po na hapon (What may happen is the trial will be held in the afternoon, keep the day schedule, or a mix of both. There will be days that it will be held in the morning and days that it will be held in the afternoon),” he said.

The scheduling changes are being considered as the impeachment court tries to maximize available trial days and accommodate the Senate’s other legislative responsibilities. Tongol said the adjustments are intended to help the impeachment proceedings meet the expected timeline for completion in December.
Tongol said the impeachment court could announce the changes as early as Wednesday.
The development came after prosecution panel adviser and former Rep. Robert Ace Barbers suggested extending the trial hours or adding hearing days to hasten the proceedings

articles.title: Juan GDL provides offensive punch in defensive duel with Iran
articles.summary: Juan Gomez de Liaño made sure to prove that his breakout performance from last window against New Zealand was far from being a fluke as he once again carried the scoring cudgels for Gilas Pilipinas…

blocks.text: Juan Gomez de Liaño made sure to prove that his breakout performance from last window against New Zealand was far from being a fluke as he once again carried the scoring cudgels for Gilas Pilipinas in a game that was dictated by tough defensive stands.

The 6-foot-1 guard came alive in the second half and fired 16 points to spearhead Gilas to a 68-56 win over Team Melli and complete a sweep of the fourth window of the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers.
“He was awesome,” said national team head coach Tim Cone who was in good spirits after the big win.
“When we needed that big stretch right there that was when he kinda took over for us and hit some shots,” he added.
Gomez de Liaño’s scoring outburst was reminiscent of his performance in Gilas’ close 106-102 loss against the Tall Blacks when he took charge late in regulation and in the first overtime.
The difference, however, his efforts finally translated into a win for the Nationals.

“I’m happy. Came out with two Ws. I’m so happy for the guys; we played so hard. The entire coaching staff, our teammates. When it comes to FIBA games, every possession counts, and just as Coach Tim said, we’re just trying to value every possession, so I’m just glad we got the W,” said the Converge star.
Cone said he would have played Gomez de Liaño with more minutes but the Gilas playmaker was also given a hard time defending against Mobin Sheikhi, who torched Gilas with 21 points.

“He was the one who had to chase that little guard around, that's what made him tired. That little guard was tireless. He was going around in circles and we had to chase him all over the place and he kinda wore us out,” said Cone
“But (Gomez de Liaño) was the guy who really stepped up for us in the guard position,” he added

articles.title: Chinese warships return to West PH Sea after brief absence in August – AFP
articles.summary: The naval fleet of China reappeared near contested features in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) following a brief disappearance last month, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) reported on Tuesday,…

blocks.text: The naval fleet of China reappeared near contested features in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) following a brief disappearance last month, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) reported on Tuesday, Sept. 1.

A total of 56 vessels belonging to the People’s Liberation Army-Navy (PLA-N) and the China Coast Guard (CCG) were tracked across Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal, Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough or Panatag Shoal), Escoda (Sabina) Shoal, and Pag-asa (Thitu) Island from August 1 to 31, according to AFP spokesperson for WPS retired admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad.

Breakdown figures showed 18 ships at Ayungin Shoal, including one navy vessel and 17 coast guard ships. Bajo de Masinloc hosted 23 vessels, split between nine navy warships and 14 coast guard cutters.
Escoda Shoal recorded nine vessels, consisting of four navy ships and five coast guard units while Pag-asa Island accounted for six ships, featuring one navy vessel and five coast guard vessels.

This tally marked a rebound from a previous weekly snapshot where naval monitoring recorded from August 18 to 24 showed zero Chinese warships, consisting entirely of 16 CCG ships stationed at Ayungin Shoal, Bajo de Masinloc, and Pag-asa Island.

When asked why the warships vanished temporarily during that mid-August window, Trinidad cautioned against drawing immediate conclusions as he noted that short-term observations fail to capture the full picture.
“We mentioned last week that monitoring over one week is still not sufficient to give us a good ground for assessment,” Trinidad said.

“What we reported last week was that there were zero monitored PLA warships. For this week, we are releasing the monthly monitoring. Probably after a month or three months, we could give a better appreciation, a better assessment,” he added.

The AFP tracked 18,534 total vessels throughout August as part of its maritime domain awareness operations inside the country’s exclusive economic zone (EEZ). This broader traffic comprised 2,545 domestic ships and 15,989 foreign vessels.
Officials issued radio challenges to 12,502 of them, while 6,032 ships did not respond to such calls.

articles.title: Peso sinks to fresh record-low ₱62.4:$1 as global risks fuel calls for clearer BSP guidance
articles.summary: Despite a fresh policy rate hike, escalating geopolitical risks and rising import costs dragged the Philippine peso to a record-low ₱62.4 to the dollar, fueling market demands for clearer guidance…

blocks.text: Despite a fresh policy rate hike, escalating geopolitical risks and rising import costs dragged the Philippine peso to a record-low ₱62.4 to the dollar, fueling market demands for clearer guidance from the central bank.
The peso slid to another historic-low close against the greenback on Tuesday, Sept. 1, from the previous record of ₱62.265 last Friday, Aug. 28. The local currency’s close was also its intraday low.

The peso opened at ₱62.25, which was also its intraday high, at the start of the week. Total trading volume fell to $1.306 billion from Friday’s $1.962 billion, according to the Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP).

Ruben Carlo O. Asuncion, chief economist at Union Bank of the Philippines (UnionBank), said the peso’s continued weakness was driven by a stronger US dollar, higher US Treasury yields, rising expectations of an interest rate hike in the US, and resurging oil prices amid re-escalating tensions in the Middle East.
“These developments have encouraged investors to shift toward dollar assets while increasing inflation and import cost concerns for oil-importing economies such as the Philippines,” Asuncion said.

MUFG Global Markets Research senior currency analyst Michael Wan noted that the Philippine peso continues to underperform. Markets were closed last Monday, Aug. 31, as the country commemorated National Heroes Day.
Diwa Guinigundo, Philippines analyst at New York-based economic think tank GlobalSource Partners, also noted in an Aug. 30 commentary that global pressures have been shaping the value of the peso.

Meanwhile, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) show of hawkishness through a policy rate hike to five percent fell short of easing market skepticism over the central bank’s determination to curb inflation. This was Guinigundo’s comment on last Friday’s record-low close, before the latest historic-low finish.

“To be sure, the peso is influenced by global dollar strength, oil prices and other external forces,” Guinigundo said. “But its immediate reaction to a rate hike is nevertheless instructive: the market did not seem fully convinced that the BSP had signaled an unambiguous commitment to staying on top of inflation.”

Guinigundo, who is a former BSP deputy governor, said the currency market’s reaction should serve as a warning, pointing out that the financial sector is looking for clearer forward guidance rather than a nominal adjustment to borrowing costs.

Guinigundo said the local currency’s continued slide “may be telling us that markets are looking beyond the 25-basis-point (bp)” rate hike, referring to whether the BSP intends to maintain elevated lending costs until price pressures ease back to the two- to four-percent tolerance range.

Asuncion expects the peso to remain strained in the near term as markets await key US economic data and the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) policy decision. “Sustained strength in the dollar, elevated global yields, and higher energy prices could keep the currency on the defensive,” he said.
“However, continued support from remittances, business process outsourcing (BPO) revenues, tourism receipts, and foreign investment inflows should help temper excessive volatility,” he added.

For the next monetary policy meeting scheduled in October, Guinigundo said the BSP will have access to ample data on prices, the currency, global oil costs, domestic demand, and inflation expectations to determine whether the policy stance remains tilted toward the hawkish.

articles.title: PAGASA warns Pampanga floodwaters may still rise from upstream runoff
articles.summary: Floodwaters in parts of Pampanga may still rise even as rainfall eases in some areas, as water from previous rains in the upstream portions of the Pampanga River Basin continues to flow downstream,…

blocks.text: Floodwaters in parts of Pampanga may still rise even as rainfall eases in some areas, as water from previous rains in the upstream portions of the Pampanga River Basin continues to flow downstream, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said.
PAGASA Hydrometeorology Division chief Engr. Socrates Paat Jr. said Pampanga, is in the lower portion of the river basin, where water from the mountains continues to add to the volume of floodwaters.

“So yung mga inulan noong nagsimula ng Thursday, Friday, ay patuloy pa rin bumababa sa ngayon, yung mga tubig na yun, yung mga volume of water na nanggaling sa bundok through the river channel (So the water from the rains that started Thursday and Friday is still coming down now, the volume of water that came from the mountains through the river channel),” Paat said in a press conference on Tuesday, Sept. 1.
Paat said this is why water levels can continue rising even after rainfall has stopped in the affected area.

“Sa ngayon po, hindi naman na gaanong marami ang pag-ulan doon sa upstream. So yun na lang yung mga inulan na yun yung hinihintay nating tuluyang makababa (At present, there is not much rainfall in the upstream areas. So we are just waiting for the water from those previous rains to completely flow down),” he said.

“Ine-expect pa rin natin na may pagtaas pa rin doon sa mga water levels at magdadagdag pa rin sa pagdurusa ng ating mga kababayan na nalubog na sa tubig (We still expect some increase in the water levels, which will add to the suffering of our fellow Filipinos who are already submerged in floodwaters),” he added.
He said PAGASA would continue monitoring weather conditions in the coming days and issue advisories if evacuation or coordination with local governments becomes necessary.
Paat further explained that flooding tends to linger in several communities in the Pampanga Delta because of their low elevation and proximity to Manila Bay.
He said the situation becomes more difficult when a large volume of water comes down from the upstream portions of the Pampanga River Basin.
He added that the low-lying communities in the Pampanga Delta can also experience stagnant floodwaters when the water level in Manila Bay is higher.

“Kaya kung mas mataas yung Manila Bay, of course, magiging stagnant yung tubig na nandun sa tinatawag na ating Pampanga Delta na yun kung saan nandun yung mga bayan ng Minalin, Macabebe, Santo Tomas (So if the water level in Manila Bay is higher, of course, the water in the Pampanga Delta, where the towns such as Minalin, Macabebe and Santo Tomas are located, will become stagnant),” Paat said.

articles.title: Real estate leaders redefine excellence at 14th PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards
articles.summary: Under the theme “Defined by Excellence,” the 14th Annual PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards gathered the nation's premier builders to celebrate 16 winning organizations across 46 competitive…

blocks.text: Under the theme “Defined by Excellence,” the 14th Annual PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards gathered the nation's premier builders to celebrate 16 winning organizations across 46 competitive categories.

This year’s edition reflected a maturing landscape where regional players actively challenge established Metro Manila conglomerates, driven by portfolio diversification, rigorous sustainability certifications, and localized placemaking.

In her opening remarks, Cyndy Tan Jarabata, chairperson of the awards in the Philippines and president of TAJARA Leisure and Hospitality Group Inc., said, “The winners of the 14th PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards represent an industry showing remarkable resilience amid prevailing global uncertainties. Against a backdrop of mounting pressures, developers adapted and stayed committed to building for the Filipino people, finding innovative ways to deliver quality homes and commercial spaces. This year, we witnessed regional developers competing at par with national players, while projects pursued rigorous sustainability and wellness certifications.”

The night’s biggest headline belonged to Cebu Landmasters, Inc. (CLI), which made history by capturing its second Best Developer title—its first since 2019. The nine-title sweep underscored CLI's transformation from a regional heavy-hitter into a formidable national real estate developer.

blocks.caption: Jose Franco B. Soberano, president and CEO of Cebu Landmasters, Inc., delivers his acceptance speech as the company takes home the Best Developer of the Year award at the PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards 2026, celebrating CLI’s legacy of excellence, service, and purpose. (Photo: PropertyG…

blocks.text: Jose Franco B. Soberano, president and CEO of Cebu Landmasters, Inc., delivers his acceptance speech as the company takes home the Best Developer of the Year award at the PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards 2026, celebrating CLI’s legacy of excellence, service, and purpose. (Photo: PropertyGuru)

In addition to winning Best Developer (Visayas) and Best Developer (Mindanao), CLI picked up trophies for Radisson RED Cebu Mandaue (Best Next Gen Hotel Development) and North Grove at Pristina Town (Best Mid End Condo Development - Metro Cebu), among other awards.

“This is to honor my father (Jose Soberano III). He started CLI [back then] with 200 houses in 2004. We’re now approaching 50,000 houses in a few months,” CLI chief executive officer Jose Franco B. Soberano said in his acceptance speech. “It has been a journey filled with a lot of hard work but strongly defined by purpose: To treat real estate as a service for our countrymen.”

Aboitiz Economic Estates, with Aboitiz Land, secured Best Developer (Luzon), alongside Best Industrial Developer, a title held for six consecutive years, recognizing the real estate group’s industry-anchored approach in creating and enabling communities across the region. The developer also bagged major titles for its estates: Best Lifestyle Housing Development for The Villages at LIMA, Best Completed Mixed Use Development for Biz Hub at LIMA, and Best Industrial Estate Development for TARI Estate.

blocks.caption: Aboitiz Economic Estates and Aboitiz Land receive the Best Developer award at the PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards 2026, recognizing its work across its property portfolio and its contribution to the country’s evolving real estate landscape. (Photo: PropertyGuru)

blocks.text: Aboitiz Economic Estates and Aboitiz Land receive the Best Developer award at the PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards 2026, recognizing its work across its property portfolio and its contribution to the country’s evolving real estate landscape. (Photo: PropertyGuru)

“For years, our strength has been industrial development, grounded in the belief that real estate should begin with the economic fundamentals: investment, infrastructure, and jobs. From that foundation, more complete communities can grow.

Now to be recognized across industrial, mixed-use, residential, sustainability, and overall development tells us that this approach is increasingly relevant beyond the category where it began. We will continue raising the benchmark for integrated development by building places where businesses can compete, people can access opportunity, and communities can grow sustainably,” said Rafael Fernandez de Mesa, president and CEO of Aboitiz Economic Estates and Aboitiz Land.

Landco Pacific Corporation dominated the luxury and eco-conscious categories, taking home Best Luxury Developer and Best Sustainable Residential Developer, with The Spinnaker earning Best Condo Development (Philippines) and Best Condo Development (Luzon).

blocks.caption: Landco Pacific takes Best Luxury Developer at the PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards 2026, reflecting its focus on premium residential and leisure developments (Photo: PropertyGuru)

blocks.text: Landco Pacific takes Best Luxury Developer at the PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards 2026, reflecting its focus on premium residential and leisure developments (Photo: PropertyGuru)

Erickson Y. Manzano, president and CEO of Landco Pacific Corporation, said, “These awards validate the direction we're already on, and they give us the confidence to go bigger. You'll see this philosophy scaled into larger, even more iconic resort-caliber master plans, not just single towers or enclaves, but destinations in their own right."

Jules Kay, managing director of PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards, emphasized that these developments are actively redrawing city skylines and establishing new benchmarks for liveability despite global market headwinds. “The PropertyGuru Philippines Property Awards has produced yet another diverse and distinguished roster of winners in 2026. Even as they navigate persistent global headwinds, these high-achieving developers are demonstrating what resilience looks like in Philippine real estate through adaptive design and operational excellence. From established household names to rising regional players, this year’s recipients are synonymous with an industry that continues to attract international investment.”

The recognition doesn't end in Manila. Country winners now prepare to represent the Philippines on the regional stage at the PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards Grand Final in Bangkok, Thailand, on December 11, 2026.
